name: Payfare
note: Payfare is an earned wage access platform offering digital banking and payment solutions for gig and contract workers. Fiserv is acquiring it in an all-cash deal expected to close in the first half of 2025, after Payfare lost its largest client, DoorDash, and its share price fell more than 75 percent.

name: cPaperless (SafeSend)
note: SafeSend, founded in 2008, automates the last mile of tax returns, including assembly, review, e-signature, and delivery, and integrates with tools like CCH Axcess and UltraTax CS. Thomson Reuters acquired it in cash for $600 million USD, and it expects SafeSend to generate about $60 million in 2025 revenue.

name: BrainBox AI
note: BrainBox AI makes AI software that optimizes HVAC systems to cut energy use and emissions in commercial buildings. Trane Technologies completed its acquisition of the company, which was announced in mid-December, with terms undisclosed and all 190 employees retained in Montréal.

name: Valsoft Corporation
note: Valsoft acquires and develops vertical market software companies, with a portfolio spanning more than 40 verticals. The all-equity growth round will fund further acquisitions and expansion into new geographies and industries, following 25 acquisitions in 2024.

name: Carbon6 Technologies
note: Carbon6, which builds an all-in-one software platform for Amazon merchants, is being acquired by Minneapolis-based SPS Commerce. About 40 percent of the price is paid in SPS Commerce stock, and the deal is expected to close in Q1 2025.

name: Shop.ca
note: Shopify bought the shop.ca and shop.us domains from Emerge Commerce, which had left them idle since relaunching shop.ca in 2018. The domains will now redirect users to Shopify's Shop app.

name: Trelica
note: Trelica is a UK-based SaaS access management startup whose shadow IT discovery technology helps security teams find and manage unmanaged apps. Toronto-based 1Password acquired Trelica in a cash-and-stock deal that closed Dec. 30 and brought in Trelica's entire 23-person team, with financial terms undisclosed.

name: Aspect Biosystems
note: Aspect Biosystems designs 3D-printed living tissue implants, made from stem-cell-derived cells and hydrogel biomaterials, to replace diseased tissue such as insulin-producing beta cells for Type 1 diabetes. The Series B will fund its first human clinical trials and bring total funding to over USD 260 mil.

name: Humi
roundsize: north of CAD 100 mil (company estimate; sources told BetaKit CAD 155 mil)
note: Humi, a Toronto-based HR, benefits, and payroll platform, was acquired by Australian HR software company Employment Hero, which is looking to expand into Canada. The price was paid in a mix of cash and equity and was not officially disclosed, though sources cited a CAD 155 million value.

name: Lexop
note: Lexop provides automated communication and payment collection tools for credit unions, financial institutions, and enterprise lenders. Santa Clara-based Eltropy acquired Lexop for an undisclosed amount, and Lexop will operate under the Eltropy brand while keeping its Montréal office.

name: Oxford Cancer Analytics (OXcan)
note: OXcan is a doctor-led, pre-revenue medtech startup developing a proteomics and AI-based blood test to detect early-stage lung cancer. The all-equity Series A brings its total funding to about $16.7 million USD.

name: Gumloop
note: Gumloop, founded in Vancouver, builds an AI-powered no-code workflow automation platform that connects tools like Google Sheets, Slack, and email through a drag-and-drop interface. The all-equity Series A, which the company says it raised as it relocates to San Francisco to hire, gives Nexus Venture Partners a board seat.

name: Float
note: Float provides corporate cards and spend management software for Canadian businesses, with a high-yield account product. The all-equity Series B brings its total external equity to about CAD 124 mil, and Float says the round was valued above USD 200 mil including funds received, though the company is not yet profitable.

name: League
note: League operates a white-label customer experience platform for healthcare providers and payers, including insurers such as Highmark Health and Manulife. It secured a US$100M credit facility from RBCx as it reached 40 million users under contract, and the financing will fund platform development, sales, and potential M&A.

name: Lighthouse Labs
note: Lighthouse Labs, a tech education company founded in 2013 that teaches cybersecurity, data science, analytics, and web development to mid-career learners, was acquired by Kitchener-Waterloo workforce training platform Uvaro for an undisclosed amount. Lighthouse will operate as a Uvaro subsidiary with its roughly 40 employees, and its CEO Jeremy Shaki becomes Uvaro's chief revenue officer.

name: Vasco
note: Vasco is an AI-powered revenue operations platform that unifies sales, marketing, and customer success data to help startups and scaleups fix go-to-market problems. The all-equity, all-primary seed round will fund AI enhancements and global client expansion.

name: Lyteflo
note: Lyteflo offers a SaaS EV Revenue Platform that displays EV savings, incentives, and charging data on dealership websites to help dealers sell electric vehicles. The all-equity seed round closed Dec. 3 and follows an initial $700,000 SAFE round.

name: The51
note: The51, a women-led investment firm, held the final close of its CAD 51 million Food and AgTech Fund, which invests $350,000 to $2 million in pre-seed and Series A startups using technologies like AI, robotics, and biotech. The close came after nearly four years of fundraising, and the fund has already invested in six companies.

name: Moment Energy
note: Moment Energy makes battery energy storage systems from repurposed EV batteries to help off-grid customers cut diesel use. The Series A will help fund its planned gigafactory in Taylor, Texas and double the size of its Vancouver headquarters.

name: Basetwo
note: Basetwo sells an AI copilot for chemical and pharmaceutical manufacturing engineers that combines plant data with physics and chemistry principles to cut energy use, costs, and cycle times. The all-equity Series A brings its total raised to USD 17.5 mil, and the funds will go toward developing the copilot and an autonomous control feature called AutoPilot.

name: Novacap Digital Infrastructure Fund
note: Montréal-based private equity firm Novacap closed its first fund dedicated to digital infrastructure, exceeding its $750-million USD target after two years of fundraising. The fund has already invested in four companies and plans up to $100 million into about 10 regional connectivity and data access businesses.

name: Street Context
note: Street Context provides content distribution and email intelligence tools that help sell-side brokerages manage research and track engagement. It was acquired by BlueMatrix, an investment research publishing platform, for an undisclosed amount, and the combined company aims to unify authoring, financial data, and analytics.

name: MolecuLight
note: MolecuLight makes handheld devices that use fluorescent light to detect and measure bacteria in wounds and surgical sites. The company raised the financing from Hayfin as sole investor to expand globally and develop thermal imaging and 3D wound visualization features, though the equity and debt split was not disclosed.

name: Clay
note: Clay makes AI software that automates customer research and sales and marketing outreach, and its customers include OpenAI, Canva, and Anthropic. The USD 40 million round at a USD 1.25 billion valuation makes it a unicorn, less than a year after its USD 46 million Series B at USD 500 million.

name: Optable
note: Optable makes data clean room software that lets advertisers and publishers aggregate, anonymize, and compare user data to measure campaign performance. The USD 20 million (about CAD 28.8 million) round was classified as a Series A extension and included USD 6 million in venture debt.

name: Nue
note: Nue builds revenue lifecycle management software for quotes, customer lifecycles, billing, and revenue, built on Salesforce's CPQ platform as an alternative to Salesforce CPQ. The all-equity Series A brings its total raised to about USD 40 mil.

name: Offstreet
note: Offstreet makes licence plate-based parking validation software for universities, healthcare centres, and parking operators. Its $2.4-million all-equity seed round, its second seed, was Conexus Venture Capital's first investment from its $30-million Fund II.

name: OneVest
note: OneVest offers a modular, end-to-end wealth management software platform for financial institutions such as banks, asset managers, and credit unions. The all-equity Series B brings its total funding to about $53 million CAD and will fund product development and US expansion.

name: Paywiser Japan (Japanese subsidiary of Paywiser)
note: Montréal-based Nuvei acquired the Japanese subsidiary of British payments company Paywiser, gaining a Japanese acquiring licence from METI. The deal lets Nuvei offer direct acquiring across major card schemes and expand alternative payment method connectivity in Japan, with the new Tokyo headquarters joining its offices in Asia-Pacific.

name: Sound Blade
note: Sound Blade has developed a handheld ultrasound device that uses histotripsy to non-invasively destroy liver tumours, both cancerous and benign. The $16.5 million USD ($23.8 million CAD) Series A will fund team expansion and development toward eventual clinical use.

name: VueReal
note: VueReal makes microprinting technology that aims to improve yield, efficiency, and cost in microLED and micro semiconductor manufacturing. The all-primary, all-equity Series C closed in December from existing investors, with EDC leading and Samsung Ventures exiting the cap table.

name: Mangrove Lithium
note: Mangrove Lithium uses an electrochemical process to refine raw lithium from brines, hard rock, clays, and recycled batteries into battery-grade lithium hydroxide or carbonate. It closed strategic financing to start construction of a refining plant in British Columbia, slated to be operational later this year.

name: FLiiP
note: FLiiP provides an all-in-one SaaS platform for fitness business management, targeting multi-location commercial gyms in North America and Europe. The all-equity seed round was led by St. Louis-based Cultivation Capital, with participation from Boreal Ventures and angel investors, and the company plans to use it to expand into the U.S. and add AI reporting features.

name: StackAdapt
note: StackAdapt is a Toronto-based demand-side advertising platform used by thousands of brands and agencies. The all-equity round values the company near $2.5 billion USD, and The Globe and Mail reported it was mostly secondary, which StackAdapt declined to confirm.

name: Rayhawk Technologies
note: Rayhawk makes sensor-guided crane-like systems that automate opening, inspecting, closing, and sealing cargo railcar lids, removing workers from hazardous work on top of railcars. The all-equity seed round is the company's first external equity round and will fund commercialization and scaling to grain terminals, food processing, ports, and mining sites.

name: RetinaLogik
note: RetinaLogik makes a portable VR and AI-based eye test platform used by optometry and ophthalmology clinics to collect and analyze visual field data. The company closed a CAD 1.1 million convertible note extension to its pre-seed round and received Health Canada Class II medical device licence, enabling monitoring and diagnostics use.

name: LavaReach
note: LavaReach, a bootstrapped Toronto startup founded in 2023, built an AI tool that researches lists of prospective companies from plain-language questions to help sales teams. San Francisco-based Landbase acquired it for an undisclosed amount, and LavaReach's founders will join Landbase, with the process reportedly completed within a week.

name: GTMfund
note: GTMfund, an operator-led VC firm that backs early-stage B2B SaaS startups in the US and Canada, closed its second fund at $54 million USD, above its $50 million target. The fund plans to back about 40 startups with cheques of $500,000 to $1.5 million, focusing on pre-seed and seed stages.

name: Thomson Reuters Ventures (TRV) Fund 2
note: Thomson Reuters launched its second corporate venture fund to invest in early-stage technology companies, focusing on legal, tax, accounting, risk, fraud, compliance, media, and fintech. The fund is sourced entirely from Thomson Reuters' balance sheet and plans 20 to 25 investments over three years, with cheques of USD 4 to 7 mil.

name: Alexi
note: Alexi builds AI litigation software that helps lawyers draft research memos, identify legal issues and arguments, and automate routine tasks. The company secured CAD 4.5 million in venture debt to fund growth, product development, and expansion with law firms across North America, eight months after a CAD 15 million Series A led by Drive Capital.

name: Clutch
note: Clutch is an online marketplace for buying and selling used vehicles, with reconditioning facilities that inspect and refurbish the cars it buys. The all-equity Series D values the company just above its former peak of CAD 575 million, a major recovery from its 2023 down round to $15 million.

name: Coral
note: Coral is a virtual menopause care platform offering app-based assessments, at-home or clinic blood tests, nurse-led treatment plans, and wellness coaching from perimenopause through post-menopause. The all-equity seed round closed at the end of last year and will fund platform development, marketing, and expansion to a team of eight with plans to be active nationwide by year-end.

name: Longbow Capital
note: Longbow Capital is a Calgary private equity firm investing in energy transition and power businesses in North America. The Canada Growth Fund committed up to CAD 50 million to its second Energy Transition Fund, which is targeting CAD 250 million after a CAD 150 million initial close.

name: BDC Capital (Growth Venture Fund and Growth Equity Partners)
roundsize: Nearly $1 billion ($500 million to GVF, $450 million to GEP)
note: BDC Capital, the venture arm of the Business Development Bank of Canada, committed about $1 billion across two later-stage vehicles, the Growth Venture Fund ($500M, now including co-investments) and Growth Equity Partners ($450M). The move aims to close a late-stage funding gap that the bank says nearly halved in 2023.

name: Certn
note: Certn provides an AI-powered software platform for pre-employment background screening, helping businesses hire faster while managing risk. It raised $30 million from BDC Capital's Growth Venture Fund to expand its AI-powered background checks (the same article reports Quadshift raising C$23 million in a separate round).

name: Glassbox
note: Glassbox is building an AI-powered platform to replace Excel for financial modelling and deal analysis, with its FinScript framework letting users build models from plain-text instructions. The company closed a CAD 1.65 million pre-seed round via SAFE, co-led by StandUp Ventures and FinTech Collective with support from Watertower Ventures, bringing total funding to CAD 1.85 million.

name: Reverb Therapeutics
note: Reverb Therapeutics is developing its Amplify•R platform, which uses bispecific antibodies to redirect the immune system's endogenous cytokines toward cancer or autoimmune targets. The all-equity seed round will advance its lead program AMP01 to the candidate stage.

name: Hyperlume
note: Hyperlume makes microLED-based interconnects and power circuitry to relieve connectivity bottlenecks in AI and accelerated-computing data centres, claiming 10x computing performance, 5x power savings, and 4x lower cost than copper. The oversubscribed seed round will fund product, engineering, and R&D expansion.

name: Dispersa
note: Dispersa uses fermentation to turn food waste into PuraSurf, a biosurfactant that can replace fossil-fuel and palm-derived surfactants in cleaning products. The all-equity seed round, led by Nàdarra Ventures, was financed entirely by Canadian investors and brings the company's total funding to over CAD 13 million.

name: JustEat Takeaway
note: Amsterdam-based food delivery company JustEat Takeaway, parent of Winnipeg-based SkipTheDishes, is being taken private by Prosus Group for 20.30 euros per share in cash, a 63% premium to its prior close. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2025.

name: Opal
note: Opal builds Opal Spend, an all-in-one expense management platform and ad spend credit card for advertising agencies, covering contracts, invoicing, and payments. The $1.5M pre-seed round was raised via SAFE, closed in Q4 2024, and marks the company's first funding.

name: Paperplane Therapeutics
note: Paperplane makes therapeutic VR games and headsets that reduce pain and anxiety in dental and medical settings as a drug-free alternative to sedatives. The $1.5M CAD seed round was an all-equity SAFE that also drew in Investissement Québec, CABHI, and Cedars-Sinai's IP company.

name: Venn (formerly Vault)
note: Venn, formerly Vault, is an all-in-one financial platform for Canadian businesses offering multi-currency accounts, global accounts, spend management, transfers, and accounting automation. The all-equity Series A will fund hiring to triple its 12-person team and expand products, including credit card payments for receivables and possibly lending.

name: Merchkit
note: Merchkit is building an AI platform that automates product data entry, content creation, and catalogue management so retailers, marketplaces, and brands can launch listings faster. The company closed a CAD 2 million pre-seed round via a SAFE, its first outside financing, and counts Lowe's among its customers.

name: TandemLaunch
note: Montréal venture studio TandemLaunch closed its fourth fund for early-stage deep tech startups at more than CAD 37 million, after a $27 million first close in July 2024. The Government of Canada's VCCI committed $6.5 million as part of the final close, and the fund aims to launch 15 new Montréal tech companies.

name: Holt Xchange
note: Holt Xchange, a Montréal FinTech seed-stage VC firm, is raising the final USD 2.5 million of a USD 10 million target for its Fund I, using FrontFundr's exempt-market platform and accredited investors. The fund has reportedly secured nearly USD 7.5 million from 86 LPs, and the capital will go toward follow-on support for top portfolio companies.

name: Cashew
note: Cashew, an AI market research solution, won the largest award at the third annual DMZ Women Innovation Summit pitch competition. Its $190,000 came from DMZ Ventures ($150,000) and angel network The Firehood, and three other women-led startups (Migranium, Edie Farming, Metronome) received $535,000 combined in total.

name: Dcbel
note: Dcbel makes Ara, a bidirectional home EV charging and energy management system that uses vehicle-to-home charging and AI to cut energy costs and support renewable use. The Canada Growth Fund led the USD 55 mil round to help Dcbel commercialize in North America and Europe; the CGF invested USD 40 mil directly, with other investors contributing up to USD 15 mil.

name: Paved
note: Paved is a newsletter advertising platform that connects newsletter creators with advertisers, reaching 253 million subscribers across more than 3,000 publishers. Victoria, BC-based software rollup Redbrick acquired Paved for an undisclosed amount, its fourth major acquisition in five years.

name: Pocketed
note: Pocketed is a platform that connects businesses to eligible grants and tax credits, including SR&ED, and helps them with applications. Deloitte Canada acquired the company for an undisclosed amount, and Pocketed will operate as "Pocketed, a Deloitte business" within its Gi3 practice.

name: Augmenta
note: Augmenta is developing an AI platform that automates building design, starting with electrical systems, to help contractors and engineers produce compliant plans faster and cheaper. The company closed an additional US$10 million (CAD $14.4 million) seed round via a simple agreement for future equity, bringing total funding to nearly CAD $37 million.

name: Novarc Technologies
note: Novarc makes AI-powered vision systems for autonomous welding robots, including its Spool Welding Robot and the upcoming NovAI adaptive welding system. The Series B round totals USD 50 million (CAD 71.6 million), including a USD 20 million debt component.

name: 3D at Depth
note: 3D at Depth provides underwater LiDAR technology and services for subsea assets and infrastructure, such as detecting leaks on oil rigs. St. John's-based Kraken Robotics completed the acquisition on April 2, 2025, for $17 million USD ($24.5 million CAD), subject to adjustments for debt and working capital.

name: Phoenix
note: Phoenix is a Toronto digital health platform that lets men across Canada get virtual treatment for erectile dysfunction, weight management, and hair loss, with physician review and home delivery of prescriptions. The $50M CAD combines primary equity led by Valspring Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, and venture debt from CIBC Innovation Banking; total funding now stands at $55M.

name: ShareDo
note: ShareDo sells legal case management software to over 40 large law firms, mostly in the UK. Burnaby-based Clio acquired it, funded with cash, stock, and debt, to enter the enterprise legal market; the price was not disclosed.

name: Softchoice
note: World Wide Technology, a St. Louis-based cloud and software solutions provider, completed its take-private acquisition of Toronto-based Softchoice at $24.50 per share. Softchoice will keep its name and CEO Andrew Caprara.

name: Vantage Discovery
note: Vantage Discovery is an AI-powered search platform for retailers that offers semantic search and personalization to move beyond keyword matching. Canadian e-commerce company Shopify acquired the startup for an undisclosed amount, and Shopify says the team will help improve search for merchants and buyers.

name: Ownright
note: Ownright (formerly Doormat) provides tech-enabled legal services for residential real estate closings, mortgage refinancing, and status certificate reviews in Ontario. The all-equity seed round, closed in late December, brings its total funding to CAD 6.5 mil including a CAD 1.25 mil pre-seed.

name: Summit Nanotech
note: Summit Nanotech uses nanomaterials and a data analytics platform for direct lithium extraction from brine, with its patented denaLi product. The funding will help it move from demonstration to commercial-scale design, following a demonstration plant commissioned in Northern Chile.

name: Page
note: Page is an AI platform that tracks government activity, policy changes, and legislation across Canada for organizations to monitor and influence. The all-equity seed round closed in February, bringing its total funding to more than CAD 5.5 mil, and the startup plans to use it for hiring, compute, and expanding into the US and UK.

name: Sprout Family
note: Sprout Family provides employers with fertility, surrogacy, and adoption benefits, including educational resources, clinic networks, telehealth, and financial support via Sprout Pay. The all-equity pre-seed round closed in October and will be used to expand go-to-market efforts, partnerships with insurers and employers, and its care team.

name: FreshBooks
note: FreshBooks is a Toronto-based cloud accounting software company. It secured $125M USD (about $179M CAD) in debt financing, which Morgan Stanley says will refinance existing debt and fund continued growth, and the same announcement named Shaheen Javadizadeh as CEO.

name: CoLab Software
note: CoLab, an engineering design collaboration platform, received $5.6 million from a partnership with the Hibernia and Hebron projects, including software subscriptions and R&D funding, to accelerate its ReviewAI product. The funding supports about 60,000 hours of local software development, with the initial ReviewAI scope targeted for completion by 2026.

name: Styx Intelligence
note: Styx Intelligence is developing a digital risk protection platform that detects and helps organizations respond to brand impersonation, phishing, and data leaks across external digital footprints. The all-equity seed round closed in October, bringing its total funding to $4.3 million including a $1.6 million pre-seed in 2023.

name: 3Gtms (3G)
note: 3G provides a transportation management platform used by shippers, third-party logistics providers, and freight brokers to plan, rate, consolidate, and route domestic truckload, LTL, and parcel shipments. Waterloo-based Descartes Systems Group acquired 3G for USD 115 million (CAD 164.4 million) in cash.

name: SRTX
note: SRTX makes Sheertex rip-resistant tights from a durable polymer and is facing US tariff pressure on its Canadian-made products. A reported $40 million financing, which has not closed, is led by past investors, and founder Katherine Homuth is stepping down as part of the deal.

name: Nanoprecise Sci Corp
note: Nanoprecise makes AI-powered predictive maintenance software that uses connected sensors to predict equipment failures in industries such as mining, oil and gas, and manufacturing. Its Series C combined equity and debt totaling USD 36 million (CAD 52 million), and the company reported ARR of $10 million in 2024, up 114% year-over-year.

name: BioAlert Solutions
note: BioAlert makes an automated device and remote software platform that continuously detects Legionella and other harmful pathogens in building water cooling systems. The company raised a $2.5-million seed round co-led by GreenSky Ventures and Cycle H20, with participation from Fondaction and Spring Impact Capital.

name: AdvancedAg
note: AdvancedAg is an Indigenous, family-owned agricultural biotech company that makes microbial seed, soil, and foliar products meant to reduce reliance on synthetic chemicals. The $2 million all-equity seed round was led solely by Raven Indigenous Capital Partners, and the company plans to use it for R&D, IP, and market expansion across North America.

name: Serato
note: Serato makes DJ software, including Serato DJ, Serato Studio, and Serato Sample. Victoria-based holding company Tiny bought a controlling 66% stake for USD 66 million (CAD 94.5 million), valuing Serato at USD 175 million and paid in a mix of cash and common shares.

name: One9
note: One9, the Ottawa-based VC firm focused on defence tech, sold its VC business to Toronto's Kensington Capital Partners, which will use it to build its own defence tech VC platform. Financial terms were not disclosed, and One9's Special Mission Fund and existing portfolio were excluded from the deal.

name: Vopemed
note: Vopemed (formerly Vope Medical) develops Claris, AI software that enhances laparoscopic and robot-aided surgery video by removing smoke and restoring areas obscured by fluids. The CAD 2.29 million pre-seed round funds development and clinical validation, with North American clearance targeted by mid-2026.

name: Osney Capital
note: Osney Capital, a UK-domiciled VC firm, closed its first fund at over 50 million pounds to back pre-seed and seed-stage cybersecurity startups in the UK and Canada. The firm plans to build a 30-company portfolio, writing first cheques of 250,000 to 2.5 million pounds, and is opening an office in Calgary.

name: Tailscale
note: Tailscale, a zero-configuration corporate VPN company founded in 2019, raised a Series C round that puts its post-money valuation at $1.45 billion USD. The all-equity round was led by Accel, with returning investors CRV, Insight Partners, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital participating.

name: Blumind
note: Blumind is a fabless semiconductor developer building an analog AI chip that processes physical signals like sound and vision to reduce power use and latency in always-on applications. The all-equity round brings its total raised to CAD 34 million, and the company plans to produce a high-volume version of its first product next year.

name: Corinex
note: Corinex provides broadband-over-power-lines grid visibility and flexibility products, including sensors and a software platform for real-time load balancing. The all-equity round was backed solely by European investors to fund deployments in Germany, Spain, and the UK, with Energy Growth Momentum and Suma Capital gaining board seats.

name: Puzzle Medical
note: Puzzle Medical develops the ModulHeart, a minimally invasive heart pump for advanced heart failure patients that could offer a less-invasive alternative to LVADs. The $43 million second Series A, closed in March and all-equity, will fund a human feasibility study and team growth from 45 to 60.

name: Xaba
note: Xaba sells an autonomous AI control system that lets humans instruct industrial robots through low-code, natural-language commands, with its xCognition and PLCfy programs generating code automatically. The all-equity seed extension, closed at the end of last year, brings its total funding to $8 million USD.

name: Cyclic Materials
note: Cyclic Materials recovers rare earth elements from EV motors, wind turbines, MRI machines, and e-waste to build a circular magnet supply chain. Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund joined via a second extension of the Series B, which had originally raised CAD 71 million in September 2024, but Amazon's investment amount was not disclosed.

name: Trillick Ventures
note: Winnipeg-based early-stage VC firm Trillick Ventures is raising a $15-million first fund to back pre-seed and seed tech startups in Manitoba. It has secured nearly $5 million toward that target and aims to close the rest by August.

name: PolicyMe
note: PolicyMe sells its own digital insurance products (term life, critical illness, health and dental) directly to consumers and white-labels its platform for other insurers. It closed CAD 30 million in previously unannounced equity and debt across three tranches since 2023, which the company labels as its Series B; it has not disclosed its valuation.

name: TruthSayer AI
note: TruthSayer AI launched an AI "Hedge Fund-in-a-Box" service that uses open-source language models to generate quantitative investment strategies for retail investors, small hedge funds, and family offices. The company has raised $400,000 CAD in seed funding so far and plans to raise more in the coming months.

name: NiaHealth
note: NiaHealth offers preventative health testing through an annual subscription, using AI insights, diagnostics, and clinician consultations to build lifestyle action plans. The $2.5M CAD pre-seed round, closed in late 2023, was disclosed as the company exited stealth and launched its beta.

name: FundThrough
note: FundThrough provides invoice factoring that lets SMBs sell unpaid invoices for upfront cash, with nearly $3 billion funded to date. The all-equity Series B came alongside its acquisition of U.S. invoicing platform Ampla, terms of which were undisclosed.

name: Fluent Ventures
note: Fluent Ventures, a San Francisco-based VC firm founded in Canada, closed a $40-million USD program that includes its first fund and a coinvestment strategy for LPs. It will invest $250,000 to $2 million USD in pre-seed to Series A FinTech, health, and e-commerce startups globally, with about 10 percent of its first fund expected to go to Canadian companies.

name: 7Gen (Seven Generation Capital)
note: 7Gen provides an EV-as-a-service platform for businesses, bundling EV leasing, charging infrastructure, and software into one monthly bill. It secured CAD 48 million in senior secured debt from UK-based Zenobē to finance 400 to 500 new commercial EVs and refinance part of its existing fleet.

name: Brio
note: Brio is a SaaS platform that centralizes and automates limited partner management for alternative asset managers, including VC, PE, real estate, and multi-family offices. The all-equity seed round was co-led by Walter Global Asset Management and Canso Innovations, and Brio spun out of Brightspark Ventures in January.

name: Axibo
note: Axibo, a Cambridge, Ontario company that started as an AI camera-mount maker and built a consumer virtual production tool, raised an all-equity round valuing it at $30 million USD to launch a humanoid robotics division. About 70 percent of the funds will go toward growing headcount from eight to nearly 30 and moving to a larger space near the University of Waterloo.

name: Reusables
note: Reusables provides a hardware-enabled SaaS platform that helps institutional cafeterias, such as university and hospital food services, replace single-use packaging with reusable containers. The all-equity seed round was co-led by Amplify Capital and StandUp Ventures, with participation from Sandpiper Ventures and Emend Vision Fund.

name: Veerum
note: Veerum builds detailed digital twins, virtual replicas of industrial assets, for oil, energy, mining, and construction clients. The company closed a CAD 12 million Series B on March 26 to upgrade its platform and scale its "visual operations" offering.

name: xTAO
note: xTAO is a startup focused on Bittensor, a decentralized blockchain marketplace for AI models and computing power, and is going public on the TSX Venture Exchange by merging with Vancouver-based Adrianna Ventures. The concurrent non-brokered private placement seeks up to USD 10 million via subscription receipts, with investors including Arca, Cadenza Capital, Digital Currency Group, and others.

name: Exterra
note: Exterra turns asbestos mine tailings into saleable minerals such as silica, nickel, and magnesium oxide, and uses magnesium oxide to store carbon dioxide. The all-equity Series A, which closed April 1, brings its total funding to $32 million and funds a planned commercial plant in Québec expected to open in 2027.

name: Unblocked
note: Unblocked builds a platform that captures the context behind code decisions by integrating with tools like Slack and GitHub, helping developers understand AI-generated code. The all-equity Series A, reported as USD 20 million (CAD 27.5 million), will fund its contextual intelligence engine and deeper tool integrations.

name: Active Impact Investments
note: Active Impact Investments, a Vancouver seed-stage climate tech VC, reached a $110M CAD final close for its third fund, nearly double the size of its second. The firm has invested in 39 companies and plans to back 18 more from Fund III, mostly in Canada.

name: Amilia
note: Amilia makes management, registration, billing, and payment software for YMCAs, JCCs, community centres, and parks and recreation agencies. The $35M round was led by Vertu Capital, with a secondary capital component, and marks Vertu's fifth investment from its inaugural fund.

name: Elevia Fund (Anges Québec)
roundsize: $1.5 million to $2 million (first-iteration target; $1 million to $3 million range)
note: Anges Québec, a network of more than 200 Québec angel investors, launched Elevia Fund, a co-investment vehicle that lets members and external investors back pre-seed and seed-stage Canadian tech companies without doing their own due diligence. The first iteration targets up to 60 investors with a $25,000 minimum, planning 8 to 10 investments averaging $150,000 each.

name: Intrepid Labs
note: Intrepid Labs uses AI and robotics (its Valiant platform) to design drug formulations in days rather than months. The $11M USD (CAD 15.4M) is cumulative, combining a $7M USD seed round and a previously unannounced $4M USD pre-seed round.

name: SRTX
note: SRTX, which makes Sheertex rip-resistant tights, has closed more than half of a $40M USD fundraising deal expected to finish in July. The raise follows founder Katherine Homuth's departure as CEO, with CFO Timothy Leyne named interim CEO.

name: Velocity Fund II
note: Velocity Fund II, spun out of the University of Waterloo's Velocity incubator, closed an initial close of USD 10 million toward a planned USD 25 million target to back pre-seed and seed startups. The University of Waterloo contributed USD 2 million (CAD 2.8 million) from its endowment, the first Canadian university to invest endowment money in venture capital.

name: Veritree
note: Veritree is a nature restoration platform spun out of Tentree that helps companies plant and verify tree projects with on-site data and monitoring. The all-equity Series A, closed in late 2024, was an up round that included some secondary capital and brings total funding to over CAD 15.4 million.

name: WonderFi
note: WonderFi operates regulated Canadian crypto exchanges Bitbuy and Coinsquare. US trading platform Robinhood is acquiring it for CAD 250 million in cash, with closing expected in the second half of 2025 pending regulatory, court, and shareholder approval.

name: Una Software
note: Una builds a financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform that helps enterprise finance teams track, forecast, and report on business financials, and it is adding AI features such as a conversational co-pilot and predictive forecasting. The all-equity round brings its total seed funding to $10 million USD ($13.9 million CAD), following a $7.5 million CAD round last December.

name: Verdi
note: Verdi retrofits existing farm irrigation systems with small IoT devices that allow growers to control, automate, and monitor watering row by row. The seed round brings its total funding to CAD 9.5 million (per the article) and will fund expansion, hiring, and AI-powered tools.

name: Novisto
note: Novisto sells ESG data collection, audit, and reporting software to large enterprises, with clients including Bell, Bombardier, Meta, and WSP. The all-equity Series C, closed in March, includes $2 million USD in secondary capital and will fund European expansion and generative AI integration.

name: Angus Reid Group
note: Angus Reid Group, a Vancouver market research and public opinion firm, is merging with Rival Group, the parent of Rival Technologies and Reach3 Insights, to form what Rival says is the largest Canadian-owned independent market research company, with projected revenue above $60M CAD and over 180 employees. The financial terms were not disclosed, and the deal is expected to close later this month.

name: Stablecorp
note: Stablecorp issues QCAD, a stablecoin pegged to the Canadian dollar. The company raised strategic growth capital to build out its CAD stablecoin rails, including on-chain FX markets and payment integrations, and to set up an independent-trustee reserve trust.

name: AssistIQ
note: AssistIQ has built an AI-powered software platform that helps hospitals track medical supplies and implants and monitor device usage to cut costs and save staff time. The all-primary, all-equity Series A closed in April and was led by Battery Ventures, with participation from Tamarind Hill.

name: WareMatch
note: WareMatch is an online marketplace and industrial leasing platform, often compared to Airbnb or Zillow, where customers can browse, compare, and book warehouse space from third-party logistics providers. The company raised CAD 2 million through a SAFE to support international expansion, with Farfill planning to help it expand into Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, Australia, and Asia Pacific.

name: Broker Online Exchange (BOX)
note: BOX is a management platform for energy brokers, offering supplier access, live pricing, and customer-management tools to more than 2,000 brokers in Alberta and the US. San Francisco-based AppDirect acquired all of BOX at an enterprise valuation of USD 85 million, closing on May 8, as part of its push into electricity and energy infrastructure.

name: Eavor
note: Eavor develops a closed-loop geothermal system that produces clean, dispatchable heat and power, with its first commercial plant under construction in Geretsried, Germany. Canada Growth Fund's second investment brings its total to about CAD 138 mil, including a further CAD 48 mil payable on undisclosed milestones.

name: Fispan
note: Fispan provides a plugin that embeds banking services into ERP and accounting systems for SMBs, with clients including BMO, TD, Wells Fargo, and JP Morgan. The Series B includes more than $17 million USD in secondary capital, mostly to early-stage backers, and Fispan is reportedly cash-flow positive with about $25 million USD in annual revenue.

name: Portless
note: Portless offers direct air shipping for small D2C orders, letting retailers defer US import duties until goods are sold, and operates a fulfillment warehouse in Shenzhen. The all-equity Series A was raised on the assumption that the US 'de minimis' exemption would be eliminated.

name: Rails
note: Rails is a hybrid crypto exchange that aims to give traders centralized-exchange performance while users keep custody of their own digital assets. The company raised $14 million USD through a token warrant sale, closed in April, bringing its total funding to about $20 million USD.

name: Untether AI
note: Untether AI, a Toronto-based maker of energy-efficient AI inference chips, has ceased supplying its products and is joining AMD under a strategic agreement, with AMD acquiring its software and AI hardware engineering employees. The financial terms were not disclosed, and Untether AI had previously raised about $152 million USD from investors including Intel, Tracker Capital, CPPIB, and Radical Ventures.

name: Taiv
note: Taiv sells targeted ads on bar, restaurant, and retail TVs through a free device that connects to existing cable boxes, and it now serves 1,000+ restaurants and bars and 1,000+ retail locations in 14 US cities. The Series A includes $7.75M USD in equity and $2.75M USD in venture debt, and it brings total funding to $16.5M USD.

name: ENVGO
note: ENVGO is developing NV1, an electric hydrofoiling cruiser that rises above the water to cut emissions and extend range, with a planned 2026 release manufactured in Ontario. The all-equity seed round was led by Two Small Fish Ventures, which gains a board seat, with participation from Garage Capital and angel investors.

name: Eli Health
note: Eli Health makes an at-home, saliva-based hormone tester that pairs a single-use cartridge with a mobile app to measure cortisol and progesterone levels. The Series A, which brings total funding to about CAD 28 million, is intended to fund the commercial launch and expand manufacturing.

name: MesoMat
note: MesoMat builds hardware-as-a-service sensors embedded in rubber tires that monitor safety, leaks, fuel cost, mileage, and temperature for commercial fleet operators. The undisclosed seed round was all equity and brought its total funding to $3.8 million USD ($5.2 million CAD), with proceeds going toward building out its sales team.

name: Vessel
note: Vessel is an AI-powered fund and investor management platform that helps general partners and limited partners automate reporting, compliance, and investor-call prep. The all-equity seed round closed in late May and was co-led by Inovia Capital and Afore Capital.

name: Applied Photophysics
note: Kitchener-Waterloo's Nicoya Lifesciences, which sells analytical instruments for biomolecular interaction analysis, acquired UK-based Applied Photophysics, a more than 50-year-old leader in biophysical characterization, in a deal that closed in May. The purchase price was not disclosed, but the deal is expected to double Nicoya's annual revenue and triple its customer base to nearly 3,000.

name: Carbon Upcycling
note: Carbon Upcycling makes alternative cement and concrete materials by combining CO2 with industrial byproducts and natural materials, and claims it can cut cement use by up to 50 percent. The company closed an $18-million USD convertible note round led by Chicago-based impact investor Builders Vision, bringing its total capital and grants raised to about $95.5-million CAD.

name: AppDirect
note: AppDirect, a B2B marketplace that sells cloud, telecom, hardware, AI and now energy services, received a $100-million credit facility to help finance its acquisitions of energy brokerages DNE Resources and Broker Online Exchange (BOX). The deal supports the company's push into North American energy markets as AI-driven power demand grows.

name: Xatoms
note: Xatoms uses quantum chemistry and neural networks to discover photocatalysts that purify water when exposed to sunlight, and it is running pilots in Texas, Kenya, and South Africa. The $3M pre-seed round consists of $2M in equity and $1M in non-dilutive grants.

name: Storytime Capital
note: Toronto early-stage VC firm Storytime Capital held the first close of its second fund, Fund II, with more than $14 million CAD in commitments. It aims to close $25 million to $30 million over the next year to back 20 pre-seed and seed-stage companies building future-of-work tech.

name: Botpress
note: Botpress builds an all-in-one platform for building and deploying LLM-powered AI agents, and it pivoted from chatbots after the rise of ChatGPT. The all-equity Series B closed in May at a $120-million USD post-money valuation, bringing total funding to $45 million USD.

name: Conquest Planning
note: Conquest Planning runs an AI-powered financial planning platform used by financial advisors and investors, including its Strategic Advice Manager (SAM) system. The Series B will fund US expansion and a new service, SAM Bytes, for investors who don't want a dedicated advisor; the round closed June 17.

name: NiaHealth
note: NiaHealth offers an annual subscription for medical tests co-signed by clinicians, covering 35 biomarkers and one-on-one clinician consultations, with plans priced at $299 to $1,299 per year. The seed round was raised entirely on a SAFE and included returning investors Version One Ventures and Wattpad co-founder Ivan Yuen.

name: CentML
note: CentML helps companies identify the hardware that can run their machine learning models faster and more cheaply. Nvidia acquired the Toronto startup for an undisclosed amount, bringing its co-founders and at least 15 engineers into Nvidia's AI software teams.

name: vLex
note: vLex offers a legal and regulatory database with Vincent, an AI search and assistant tool, serving over 2.8 million users in 100 countries. Burnaby-based Clio is acquiring vLex from Oakley Capital for $1 billion USD in a cash-and-stock deal, its largest acquisition to date, expected to close later this year.

name: D-Wave Quantum
note: D-Wave, a quantum annealing computer maker spun out of UBC, completed a $400M USD at-the-market common share offering at an average of $15.18 per share to fund acquisitions, working capital, and capex. The raise brings its cash balance to about $815M USD and is its third such offering since December 2024.

name: Kardium
note: Kardium makes the Globe Pulsed Field System, a catheter-based device for treating atrial fibrillation with pulsed field ablation. The CAD 340 million financing will fund FDA Class 3 regulatory approval, manufacturing expansion, and a commercial launch later this year, and it follows a CAD 143 million round a year earlier.

name: UniUni
note: UniUni is a gig-worker-powered last-mile delivery and e-commerce logistics platform that serves partners like AliExpress, Shein, and Temu. The all-equity Series D is its third raise in just over a year, and the company plans to use it to expand warehouses, AI capabilities, and delivery coverage in the US and Canada.

name: Barley
note: Barley is a compensation planning software platform that helps companies structure, analyze, and manage employee pay. Montréal-based Workleap acquired Barley and its six-person team, adding compensation management to its employee engagement and performance platform; financial terms were not disclosed.

name: Rivr (Botni.Vision)
note: Rivr uses AI to ingest gaming, podcast, and live event videos and make them searchable by emotional moments and highlights for creators and brands. The convertible note seed round closed in February and brings its total funding to about USD 4 mil.

name: Blue Cheetah Analog Design
note: Blue Cheetah Analog Design, a Sunnyvale, Calif.-based startup that designs analog mixed-signal chips, was acquired by AI hardware company Tenstorrent for an undisclosed amount. Tenstorrent says the deal brings analog and mixed-signal expertise in-house to support its planned chiplet products and open chiplet ecosystem.

name: LeoMed
note: LeoMed is a no-code remote patient monitoring platform that brings real-time vitals and care-plan task management to hospital teams, currently used at several Québec hospitals. The $2.75M seed round, led by cybersecurity firm Precicom, brings its total funding to about $5 million and will fund team expansion, markets outside Québec, and AI features.

name: Novari Health
note: Novari Health develops referral management, central intake, and surgical waitlist software for health systems. Toronto-based VitalHub acquired it for up to $48.6 million CAD, including $35.8 million cash, about 730,000 VitalHub shares, and up to $5 million in performance bonuses over two years.

name: Cobionix
note: Cobionix develops CODI, a collaborative medical robot that lets ultrasound technologists perform diagnostic ultrasounds remotely, with pilots in Canada, the US, and the UK. The all-equity strategic round will fund commercialization, including a planned US launch in 2026.

name: Opennote
note: Opennote is an AI learning platform that lets undergraduate students consolidate course materials and generate videos, diagrams, and workflows. The all-SAFE round closed in April, and the founders were accepted into Y Combinator's Summer 2025 batch.

name: R-Labs
note: R-Labs is a Toronto real estate venture builder that co-creates tech-enabled startups targeting housing affordability, climate resiliency, and sustainability. The CAD 3.5 million raise adds to its evergreen fund, bringing its total to CAD 28 million.

name: Airalo
note: Airalo sells eSIM data plans that let travelers connect abroad through carriers worldwide, often at lower rates than domestic roaming. The $220M USD Series C, led by CVC Capital Partners, values the company above $1 billion and makes it a unicorn.

name: mTatt
note: mTatt is building a way to measure blood test biomarkers using painless, invisible temporary microtattoos with fluorescent ink. It won the $100,000 Best of Fest prize at Startupfest 2025, an investment from an angel investor team in the form of a convertible note.

name: Asepha
note: Asepha is an agentic AI platform that automates administrative workflows for pharmacists, including OCR that reads handwritten prescriptions. The all-equity seed round, which closed last month, will fund doubling headcount and opening a New York City office.

name: Moonvalley
note: Moonvalley develops foundational AI video models, including Marey, which is trained only on licensed footage and aimed at filmmakers. The all-equity seed extension brings its total raised to $154 million USD since its 2023 founding, and the funds will go toward scaling enterprise demand.

name: GreenSky Ventures
note: GreenSky Ventures, a Toronto VC firm that backs early-stage Canadian B2B deep tech and enterprise software startups, closed its sixth fund at $23.5M CAD, its largest to date and near the top of its $20M to $25M target. The close drew more than 100 LPs, with returning LPs providing over half the commitments, and new managing partner Jeff Brunet joined after the $15M first close.

name: Trusty
note: Trusty is building an AI-powered estate planning app that helps families document and pass down personal valuables like art, collectibles, and jewellery, beyond what a will covers. The equity pre-seed round closed in May and was Trusty's first external financing.

name: Quandri
note: Quandri sells AI-enabled renewal intelligence software that automates policy servicing and renewal tasks for insurance brokers and agents in North America. The company closed an all-equity Series A-plus round of USD 12 million (CAD 16.5 million) in May, bringing its total funding to USD 22 million.

name: Define Capital
note: Define Capital is an open-ended private equity fund that acquires profitable, niche B2B software companies to grow over the long term. The debt facility from Scotiabank will let it stretch existing capital to make at least three more acquisitions, with a first U.S. deal targeted before year-end.

name: GeologicAI
note: GeologicAI uses AI, sensors, and imaging to help geologists analyze rock and core samples faster and locate mineral resources. The all-equity Series B will fund global scaling, expanded sensing technology, and growth in the Middle East, South America, and Asia.

name: Substack
note: Substack is a newsletter and subscription platform that lets independent creators publish, manage subscribers, and earn revenue for a cut of subscriptions. The $100M USD Series C values the company at $1.1B USD, roughly 24 times its reported $45M USD annual recurring revenue, and the company plans to invest in its app, publisher tools, and advertiser support.

name: OneCliq
note: OneCliq is an AI-enabled startup that aggregates consumer sentiment from social platforms like Instagram, Reddit, and TikTok to automate qualitative research. Toronto-based market research firm Dig Insights acquired it, closing earlier this month, and OneCliq's technology will become part of Dig's product offerings, including Upsiide.

name: xTAO
note: xTAO, a decentralized AI network built on the Bittensor protocol and launched by WonderFi co-founder Karia Samaroo, closed its financing through subscription receipts tied to a merger with Vancouver-based Adrianna Ventures. The round had no lead investor and was treated as a seed round, and it was followed by a TSX Venture Exchange listing on July 22.

name: Hyper
note: Hyper, co-founded by Damian McCabe and Ben Sanders, makes an AI voice tool that screens non-emergency 9-1-1 calls, routing callers to the right agency or escalating to a human. The company exited stealth with USD 6.3 million (CAD 8.5 million) in all-equity funding, led by Eniac Ventures, and plans to expand across the United States.

name: 4AG Robotics
note: 4AG Robotics builds Canadian-made robots that autonomously pick mushrooms using patented suction-cup technology, plus AI tools for crop yield and disease detection. The all-equity Series B, closed in mid-July, was led by Astanor and Cibus Capital and brings the company's total funding to over $60 million.

name: Cavelo
note: Cavelo scans, classifies, and reports on sensitive data, such as credit card and passport information, that companies need to protect, and sells through channel partners like MSPs and MSSPs. The all-equity $5-million seed extension was solely backed by Inovia Capital, which also led its 2023 seed round, and the company says it will use the funds for sales, marketing, product development, and new automated remediation and AI threat detection capabilities.

name: Mara Renewables
note: Mara Renewables makes algae-based DHA omega-3 oils as a fish-free alternative for supplements, infant formula, and fortified foods. It raised an all-equity extension from S2G Investments to fund commercialization and expansion into Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa, following its 2022 CAD 39.5 million raise.

name: Yaletown Partners (Innovation Growth Fund III)
note: Yaletown Partners, a Vancouver VC firm, closed the first close of its third Innovation Growth Fund at $100M CAD, targeting a $250M final close. The fund will back Series A and B digital infrastructure companies that drive productivity in energy, manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, and transportation.

name: DroneSense
note: DroneSense, founded in 2015, offers a "drone as first responder" platform that lets public safety agencies dispatch and control drones from a central location. Ottawa-based Versaterm acquired it for more than USD 100 million in a mix of cash and equity, and expects it to add over USD 10 million in revenue and 1,300 customers.

name: Blue J
note: Blue J provides AI-powered tax research software built on OpenAI's large language models, serving more than 2,500 organizations including KPMG, RSM, and Crowe. The Series D round reportedly valued the company at over USD 300 mil, and the company said it doubled revenue in the first half of 2025.

name: Clay
note: Clay is an AI go-to-market platform that helps sales and marketing teams find leads, contact data, and intent signals across more than 150 integrations and AI agents. The $100M Series C values the company at $3.1B USD, roughly six times its valuation from just over a year ago, and it serves more than 10,000 customers.

name: Finale Inventory
note: Finale Inventory is a cloud-based, multi-channel inventory management software provider for e-commerce businesses, with integrations for Shopify, shipping providers, and accounting systems. Waterloo-based Descartes Systems Group acquired it for up to USD 55 mil: USD 40 mil upfront plus USD 15 mil contingent on combined revenue targets over the two years after closing.

name: LiORA
note: LiORA (formerly Environmental Material Sciences) sells a soil remediation platform that combines a pollutant-sensing device, AI-driven analytics, and a hydrocarbon-degrading nutrient mix, mainly to oil and gas companies in Canada and the US. The all-equity seed round, closed in January, will fund a go-to-market push in the United States, and the company also secured $1.4 million in venture debt from RBCx.

name: Rail
note: Rail, formerly Layer2 Financial, provides stablecoin and global money movement infrastructure, including virtual accounts and automated back-office tools. San Francisco-based Ripple is acquiring it for $200 million USD in a mix of cash and equity.

name: Pathway Medical
note: Pathway Medical is a healthtech startup with an AI-powered search engine of peer-reviewed medical information used by healthcare professionals. San Francisco-based telehealth firm Doximity acquired it for $26 million USD in cash plus up to $37 million USD in additional equity grants, with the deal closing July 29.

name: Rozvelt
note: Rozvelt is developing VEKTR, a patent-pending hunting headgear with a mask that filters out odour particles from the wearer's exhaled breath, and has launched pre-sales. The company raised $450,000 from mostly Québec-based angel investors despite a difficult early-stage fundraising climate shaped by tariffs.

name: TeamLinkt
roundsize: more than USD 6 mil ($8.3 mil CAD)
note: TeamLinkt provides free sports management software for leagues, clubs, and associations, covering registration, scheduling, communications, and websites, with revenue from payment processing and in-app ads. The equity Series A closed in late July, will fund AI, payments, analytics, and North American expansion, and brings its total funding to $9.7 million CAD.

name: Uno Platform
note: Uno Platform sells a coding assistant that lets engineers build mobile, web, and desktop apps with drag-and-drop tools and AI code generation that stays transparent and enterprise-secure. The $3.5M convertible note brings its total funding to $6.5M, and the company plans to expand its team of about 20 with at least 10 new Montréal roles.

name: BinSentry
note: BinSentry makes solar-powered sensors and software that remotely monitor livestock feed inventory in silos, sold as a monthly service to feed mills and large farms. The Series C, led by Lead Edge Capital, will fund global expansion, including into Brazil, where Cargill is the exclusive distributor.

name: Cohere
note: Cohere builds large language models and its North enterprise AI platform for businesses and governments. The all-equity raise values the company at $6.8 billion USD, up 24% from its Series D last summer, and it also named Joelle Pineau as chief AI officer and Francois Chadwick as CFO.

name: Virtual Gurus
note: Virtual Gurus is a gig work platform that connects remote assistants with companies needing help with bookkeeping, marketing, and customer support, with a focus on underrepresented talent. The company closed the first tranche of its next funding round, widely expected to be a Series B, but did not disclose the amount.

name: Friendlier
note: Friendlier provides reusable plastic containers that food service operators use to replace single-use packaging, with deposits refunded at drop-off stations and containers sanitized between uses. The all-equity round is a second seed extension that will fund infrastructure, including new micro-sanitation hubs in Winnipeg and Halifax.

name: Aalo Atomics
note: Aalo Atomics is a Texas-based nuclear startup building factory-made, fleet-scale reactors (Aalo Pods) and its first plant, Aalo-X, which will include an experimental data centre. The $100M USD Series B follows a $27M USD Series A a year earlier.

name: BDC Capital (Industrial Innovation Venture Fund II)
note: BDC Capital launched a second CAD 200 million Industrial Innovation Venture Fund to back Series A-and-later startups in AgTech, advanced manufacturing, food tech, and tech for mining and oil and gas, with an expanded focus on critical minerals. The fund has already made three investments, most recently in Vancouver-based Apera AI, and is expected to back a number of companies comparable to Fund I's 20.

name: General Fusion
note: General Fusion, a Richmond, BC fusion energy developer, raised fresh financing to fund its LM26 demonstration program and reach its next milestone of fusion at 10 million degrees Celsius. The round was mostly internal, with existing and new backers including Segra Capital, PenderFund, Chrysalix, and JIMCO, and fell short of the company's $125 million USD goal.

name: Mechasys
note: Mechasys makes the XR Projector, a laser system that projects construction layout plans onto job sites with millimetre accuracy, with a companion software suite. The $23M Series A, closed in early August, brings its total funding to over $30M and will go toward scaling production and client onboarding.

name: Fey
note: Fey is a Montréal investment research platform offering earnings analysis, natural language stock screening, and a personalized news feed. Toronto-based Wealthsimple acquired Fey's three-person team and technology, with terms undisclosed, and plans to integrate its features into its investing platform.

name: Molly Studio
note: Molly Studio is a New York City design firm that has worked with Apple, Nike, and Google and has done AI-related work. Shopify acquired the firm for an undisclosed sum, and its seven designers will become founding members of Shopify's new internal Product Design Studio.

name: Astrus
note: Astrus builds AI software that automates the physical layout of analog circuits for advanced semiconductors, such as GPUs and AI chips. The seed round closed in July via a SAFE and will fund hiring and first paid pilots with Tier-1 chipmakers in early 2026.

name: Bench IQ
note: Bench IQ uses AI to analyze judicial rulings, including those without written opinions, and generate intelligence reports on judges' past approaches for litigators. The seed round includes USD 1 million in debt, and the company plans to expand coverage to US state and Canadian judges.

name: Molecular You
note: Molecular You runs a direct-to-consumer predictive health platform that measures more than 250 biomarkers from a single blood sample to score risks such as Alzheimer's and liver disease. The all-equity Series A (USD 5M, about CAD 6.9M) follows its nationwide US launch and will fund customer growth and clinical channels across North America.

name: Telus Digital
note: Telus Digital, formerly Telus International, provides customer experience management, automation, and generative AI services to enterprises. Parent Telus will acquire all outstanding shares at $4.50 USD per share in cash or parent-company stock, a raise from its original $3.40 offer, with closing expected later this year pending shareholder, regulatory, and court approvals.

name: Vistara Growth
note: Vancouver private credit firm Vistara Growth provides debt, convertible debt, and structured equity to mid- and later-stage North American tech companies. It has raised over CAD 370 million (USD 265 million) so far for its fifth technology-focused fund, which is nearing close.

name: White Star Capital
note: White Star Capital launched its North American Seed Fund to lead pre-seed and seed rounds for tech startups in Canada and the US, with a $50 million USD target. The first close raised $25 million USD, anchored by Fonds de solidarité FTQ with participation from Desjardins, Teralys, and TD Innovation Partners.

name: Ignition
note: Ignition is an AI-powered go-to-market platform that helps companies manage product marketing, including customer research, competitive strategy, and roadmapping. Vancouver-based Klue acquired Ignition's product IP for an undisclosed price, with none of its employees joining Klue, and Ignition's services wind down on Sept. 30.

name: Tetra Digital Group
note: Tetra Digital Group is the new parent of Calgary-based crypto custodian Tetra Trust, which also runs the Tetra Unity software business. The all-equity CAD 10 million raise will fund a Canadian-dollar stablecoin subsidiary and growth, and about 30% of it was secondary capital for early investors.

name: Bo
note: Bo, a Montréal startup offering a reusable container platform for food service operators, was acquired by Québec's largest recycling cooperative, Tricentris. The article says the price was in the 'seven-figure' range but does not disclose the exact amount.

name: LocusX
note: LocusX makes an AI-powered plug-in that uses large language models to find and propose fixes for programming bugs in video games, though it does not apply fixes automatically. The $3 million seed round closed at the end of July and will fund product refinement and a five-person team.

name: FeX Energy
note: FeX Energy is building a shipping-container iron reactor that stores renewable power in iron and releases it as high-temperature heat to replace diesel and other fossil fuels in mining, shipping, and remote heating. The all-equity round closed Sept. 5 and will fund its first pilot for an unnamed Ontario client.

name: ShopVision Technologies
note: ShopVision Technologies builds an AI agent that automates competitive analysis for e-commerce merchants by tracking competitors' promotions and identifying optimal campaign timing. The $4.1 million USD ($5.6 million CAD) all-equity seed round was led by Brightspark Ventures, with participation from BDC Capital and Rhino Ventures.

name: Mycroft
note: Mycroft offers agentic AI-driven security and compliance tooling for B2B SaaS startups, acting as a "security and compliance officer" that monitors cloud infrastructure, manages incidents, and prepares for audits. The all-equity seed round from June was led by Luge Capital, with Brightspark Ventures and Graphite Ventures as new investors and Ripple Ventures, DevCap, Antler, and BoxOne Ventures participating.

name: Thrive Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition (ETA) Fund
note: BDC Capital launched a CAD 50 million fund to help women entrepreneurs buy businesses from retiring owners, with $10 million for indirect PE fund investments and $40 million for direct equity in search funds, management buyouts, and self-funded ETA deals. The fund also includes an accelerator and targets more than 60 Canadian women pursuing acquisition-based entrepreneurship.

name: Simple Ventures
note: Toronto-based venture studio that builds startups in product and service gaps in Canada, with three launched companies so far (Alma Care, Harvest, Zero Collective). It has closed CAD 15 million for its first fund and is targeting a final close of CAD 18 to 20 million by end of 2025.

name: Cohere
note: Cohere builds large language models for enterprises and governments, competing with OpenAI and Anthropic. The $100M USD second close of its $500M USD round lifts its valuation to $7B USD, up from $6.8B.

name: Telegraph Ventures
note: Telegraph Ventures, a spinoff of European VC firm Telegraph Hill Capital, launched a generalist early-stage fund in Québec to back enterprise AI startups at pre-seed and seed, with plans for about 30 investments. The fund secured nearly $35 million in a first close and aims to reach $40 million by year-end.

name: eDOCS
note: OpenText sold its eDOCS legal document management unit to Utah-based NetDocuments for $163 million USD in cash, as part of its effort to focus on core AI-driven information management. The deal closed Jan. 12, 2026, and the eDOCS unit contributed about $30 million in revenue in OpenText's latest fiscal year.

name: Radical Ventures
note: Radical Ventures closed a US$650 million early-stage fund to invest in AI companies, replacing its 2023 fund and marking its fourth early-stage vehicle and sixth fund overall. The Canada Pension Plan Investment Board contributed US$75 million, and the Financial Times reported that Eric Schmidt's family office also backed the fund.

name: MAK Acquisition
note: MAK Acquisition, a Toronto-based SPAC led by former Dye & Durham executives Matt Proud and Avjit Kamboj, has filed a preliminary prospectus for a $100M USD IPO on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It plans to acquire technology businesses in niche markets such as tech-enabled services, space, and defence.

name: TransCrypts
note: TransCrypts operates a blockchain-based platform that encrypts and stores records such as employment credentials, with health records now live in nine countries. The $15M USD (about $20.9M CAD) all-equity seed round values the company at over $80M CAD and will fund expansion into educational and health records in the US and Canada.

name: Spellbook
note: Spellbook provides an AI-powered contract review and drafting platform for lawyers, integrated with Microsoft Word. The all-equity Series B brings its post-money valuation to USD 350 million and will fund expansion beyond contract review and growth of its go-to-market team.

name: 1Password
note: 1Password makes password and credential management software and is adding tools for securing AI agents' logins. The USD 100 million was a secondary share sale at the company's USD 6.8 billion valuation, not new primary capital, with about USD 75 million bought by Halo Fund through founders and employees.

name: ABK Biomedical
note: ABK Biomedical develops Eye90 microspheres, which are X-ray visible particles used in Y90 radioembolization to treat liver cancer and support diagnostic imaging. The USD 35 million Series D (about CAD 49.1 million) will fund clinical operations and prepare the Eye90 microspheres for commercialization.

name: Dominion Dynamics
note: Dominion Dynamics builds a platform that connects off-the-shelf sensors across land, sea, air, and space into a data fabric for allied coordination, focused on Arctic surveillance. The $4 million pre-seed was raised on a SAFE and backed mostly by Canadian investors, including Golden Ventures, Garage Capital, Afore Capital, and Side Door Ventures.

name: Provision
note: Provision builds AI co-pilots that help construction estimators find information and flag risks in complex project documents during pre-construction. The seed round, closed in August, brings its total funding to USD 8.7 mil, and the company reports over $1 million in ARR.

name: Spring Impact Capital
note: Spring Impact Capital, a Vancouver impact VC launched in 2023, closed its first fund with $14M CAD in commitments, falling short of its $20M target. The fund plans to back up to 25 pre-seed and seed climate and healthtech startups with cheques of $250K to $400K.

name: Ready Plan Go
note: Ready Plan Go is building an AI-powered back office platform that automates document collection, data extraction, and tax software form entry for accountants, and it also acquires books from retiring tax firms, starting with US firms. The $750K pre-seed round includes a cheque from Mistral Venture Partners and 15 angel investors from Montréal's startup ecosystem.

name: Fonds Impulsion
note: Investissement Québec has launched Fonds Impulsion, a $200-million VC fund targeting pre-seed and seed tech startups headquartered in Québec, replacing the shuttered Impulsion PME program. The fund plans to invest in roughly 70 companies over about 10 years, writing cheques of $250,000 to $2 million.

name: Cybrid
note: Cybrid sells payment infrastructure that lets businesses integrate stablecoin and cross-border transactions, and it recently became a payment service provider registered with the Bank of Canada. The all-equity, all-primary Series A closed six weeks before the announcement, and the company plans to expand into Europe.

name: Felix Health
note: Felix Health is a Toronto-based virtual health platform offering treatments for conditions like acne, contraception, hair loss, and weight management across most of Canada. The company raised $53 million in growth financing, a roughly equal mix of equity and debt, after reporting profitability in July and an annual run rate of $150 million CAD.

name: Loon
note: Loon is a newly formed company spun out of Toronto's Paytrie to take over and grow CADC, a Canadian dollar-backed stablecoin, which it is acquiring. The pre-seed round closed at CAD 3 million and will fund product development, compliance hiring, and engagement with Canadian securities regulators.

name: Wealthsimple
note: Wealthsimple, a Toronto-based investing and banking platform that started as a robo-adviser, signed a Series E of up to CAD 750 million at a $10 billion post-money valuation, double its valuation a year ago. The round includes a $550 million primary offering and up to $200 million in secondary, and is expected to close in Q4.

name: Maple Bridge Ventures
note: Maple Bridge Ventures, an Ottawa VC firm, closed a first close of $10.2 million CAD for its debut fund, which backs pre-seed and seed immigrant-led tech startups in agriculture, food, health, and enterprise. The fund is targeting $20 million in total.

name: Maket
note: Maket offers an AI-powered platform that helps homeowners, architects, and builders generate residential floor plans and visualizations during early design. The company raised a CAD 3.4 million seed round ahead of a 2.0 release planned for Q1 2026.

name: Magnum Capital Partners
note: Magnum Capital Partners is a Montréal private equity fund, Canada's first women-led PE fund using the search fund model, backing entrepreneurs who acquire profitable businesses. BDC's Thrive ETA Fund made its first investment in the search fund asset class with this USD 2 million commitment, toward Magnum's first fund targeting roughly USD 20 million.

name: Maritime Launch Services
note: Maritime Launch Services is building Spaceport Nova Scotia near Canso to offer satellite launch services. The $10-million senior credit facility from Export Development Canada will fund the spaceport's next construction phase, including launch pad and infrastructure.

name: Sparrow BioAcoustics
note: Sparrow BioAcoustics makes the Stethophone app, which turns smartphones into medical-grade stethoscopes with patented bioacoustics technology. The all-equity CAD 10 million round will fund scaling the platform across hospitals in North America, with the company working with most key US health systems.

name: Gander Social
note: Gander Social is building a sovereign Canadian social network as an alternative to X and Meta, with a subscription model and no surveillance ads. It raised over $1 million in the first phase of an equity crowdfunding campaign on FrontFundr from more than 1,300 investors, ahead of a planned 2026 public launch.

name: Maritime Launch Services
note: Maritime Launch is building Spaceport Nova Scotia near Canso, NS, which will offer satellite launch services to Canadian and global clients. MDA Space bought its equity stake at $0.223 per share, a roughly 50% premium to the pre-announcement price, and gained a board nomination right and pro-rata participation in future financings.

name: Beacon Software
note: Beacon acquires and partners with niche software and services firms, embeds AI into them, and grows them long term, claiming over 30% of its companies are Canadian. The all-equity Series B values the company at $1 billion and brings its total funding to $335 million.

name: Flare
note: Flare provides threat exposure management software that monitors the open internet and dark web for cybercrime such as leaked credentials and data leaks. The $30M USD total includes a $15M USD primary equity Series B extension and $15M in debt from the Bank of Montréal, bringing Flare's total equity funding to $55M USD.

name: Beyond ADHD
note: Beyond ADHD is a digital platform offering ADHD assessment, diagnosis, follow-up care, and support for related needs like depression and anxiety. Toronto-based virtual care provider Maple acquired it as a subsidiary, with terms not disclosed and all services and staff continuing within the company.

name: FrontlineIQ
note: FrontlineIQ builds an AI assistant (Theo) that gives in-person retail sales reps targeted performance feedback from sales-pitch audio and helps managers coach their teams. The $3.3 million seed round, raised via SAFEs, closed last month, and the valuation was not disclosed.

name: Clio
note: Clio sells practice-management software that helps lawyers handle client intake, case and document management, and payments, and is adding AI to complete legal tasks. It closed a $500M USD all-primary Series G at a $5B USD post-money valuation, alongside a $350M USD debt facility, to finance its $1B USD acquisition of vLex.

name: Digitail
note: Digitail sells veterinary practice software, including inventory, scheduling, a pet-owner app, and AI tools for summarizing patient records and transcribing visits. The all-equity Series B, led by Five Elms Capital, will fund product development and go-to-market hiring as the company expands in North America, where its new Toronto hub will be the base for that work.

name: CoLab Software
note: CoLab makes an AI-powered collaboration tool that lets engineering teams upload, review, and edit 2D and 3D CAD files and captures design knowledge across a company. The $72M USD (about $101M CAD) Series C was led by Intrepid Growth Partners, with the round reportedly valuing the company at around $500M USD, though CoLab did not confirm the valuation.

name: NLPatent
note: NLPatent is a Toronto legaltech startup whose AI-based patent search and analytics platform serves more than 2,000 IP and R&D professionals at law firms, Fortune 500 companies, and universities. The $3 million USD all-equity, all-primary round closed in September, co-led by Draper Associates and Mighty Capital with participation from existing backers including The LegalTech Fund, Storytime Capital, and The51.

name: Glowtify
note: Glowtify is an AI-powered marketing platform, described as a "command centre" for small e-commerce marketing teams, that automates marketing insights and content creation. The all-equity seed round closed in August and will fund go-to-market expansion ahead of the holiday season and AI engineering hires.

name: TuneIn
note: TuneIn provides radio, podcast, and music streaming to over 75 million monthly listeners across more than 200 platforms, including in-car systems. Montréal-based Stingray will pay USD 150 mil upfront, funded by a term loan, plus up to USD 25 mil 12 months after closing, with completion expected by year-end pending TuneIn shareholder approval.

name: Vessel
note: Vessel is an AI-powered fund and investor management platform that automates fundraising workflows and centralizes investor data for venture and PE firms.
