CIBC Innovation Banking provided $1.5 million in growth capital in October to support expansion in North America and Europe, following a $10.3 million CAD seed round in June co-led by Inovia Capital and Afore Capital.

name: Vistara Growth
note: Vancouver-based private credit firm Vistara Growth closed its fifth fund at USD 321 million, below its USD 386 million target but 66% larger than Fund IV. The firm will focus on mid- and later-stage North American tech companies and plans to return to market for a larger sixth fund in late 2026.

name: CereCura Nanotherapeutics
note: CereCura is a pre-clinical biotech spun out of UBC using lipid nanoparticle RNA technology to deliver therapeutic proteins across the blood-brain barrier, initially targeting neuronopathic Gaucher disease with programs for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. The all-equity seed round, closed in September and led by WUTIF Capital, brings total funding to $2.2 million.

name: Emmetros Limited
note: Emmetros, a Kitchener-Waterloo company that makes the SparxConnect patient engagement platform, is being acquired by FluidAI Medical, which is buying its assets. FluidAI plans to use Emmetros' technology to upgrade its Stream Inara AI platform for post-surgery patient recovery, and the deal terms have not been disclosed.

name: FirstList
note: FirstList built a platform that lets brokerages and agents share "coming soon" listings that are not yet on the MLS. Real estate tech platform myAbode, a tech brand of RealServus, acquired its assets for an undisclosed amount and hired co-founders Derek Hooper and Andrew Paliga along with the team.

name: MedReddie
note: MedReddie runs a platform that gives hospital and GPO procurement teams a centralized vendor list with regulatory, clinical, and performance data, and it generates RFPs in minutes. The company raised $1.55 million in equity seed funding plus an additional $500,000 in federal and provincial grants to expand into Europe and Mexico.

name: Augmentt
note: Augmentt builds a platform, optimized for Microsoft, that helps managed service providers monitor and manage security and compliance across SMBs' SaaS applications. The $18 million CAD Series A will fund product development, go-to-market efforts, and partnerships.

name: Morphocell Technologies
note: Morphocell regenerates tissues and organs, with its ReLiver stem cell-derived therapy aimed at promoting liver regeneration as an alternative to transplants. The Series A was rounded out at USD 50 million (CAD 70 million), with a USD 10 million extension on top of the USD 40 million initial close from April 2024.

name: Conexus Venture Capital (CVC)
note: Regina-based early-stage VC firm CVC closed its second fund at its CAD 30 million target, focused on pre-seed to Series A Saskatchewan software startups. Its anchor LP, Conexus Credit Union, contributed CAD 15 million, with the remainder coming from eight other undisclosed Saskatchewan institutions, high-net-worth individuals, and family offices.

name: PC Financial
note: EQB, the parent of Equitable Bank and owner of EQ Bank, acquired PC Financial from Loblaw, combining two digital-first banks and making EQ Bank the exclusive financial partner of the PC Optimum rewards program. The update says the deal has closed, and it adds 17 million PC Optimum members and about 3.5 million banking customers to the combined bank.

name: Xposure Music
note: Xposure Music buys indie artists' song catalogues and uses streaming data and AI to predict which songs will keep earning royalties. The USD 42.5 million raise combines debt and equity to fund more catalogue purchases, with a focus on Canadian artists.

name: ConstructionClock
note: ConstructionClock is a Winnipeg app that automates labour time and attendance tracking for construction subcontractors using geolocation clock-in and clock-out. The founder plans to use the CAD 2 million seed round to triple its customer count in 2026 and expand into paying workers based on verified time.

name: General Fusion
note: Richmond, BC-based General Fusion is developing magnetized target fusion to produce zero-carbon power. The company raised $51.5 million CAD, mostly via SAFEs, from 67 undisclosed investors, and PenderFund reportedly expects it to pursue a public listing, possibly through a SPAC merger.

name: Nfinite
note: Nfinite, a University of Waterloo spinout, coats paper with a nanotech thin film to make flexible packaging last longer while staying compostable and recyclable. The CAD 4.6M is a non-dilutive grant from the National Research Council of Canada's Industrial Research Assistance Program to help it move from pilot to a commercial factory.

name: Gander Social
note: Gander is building a Canadian alternative to Meta and X, hosted on Canadian servers and built on open protocols like AT. The company surpassed $1.5 million in equity crowdfunding through FrontFundr, with about $300,000 more processing, for a likely total near $2 million.

name: Inovia Capital (Fund VI and Discovery Fund II)
note: Inovia Capital is preparing to raise a sixth venture fund targeting seed to Series B companies, plus a second Discovery fund that invests in other VC funds and early-stage startups. The article describes these as planned raises with no target size or close announced, alongside the promotion of Kory Jeffrey and Taha Mubashir to partner.

name: Assetflo
note: Assetflo sells IoT software and hardware that uses mesh networking and existing infrastructure, such as Wi-Fi routers, to track the location and condition of physical assets indoors and outdoors. The equity seed round closed in August and brings its total VC funding to about USD 3 million.

name: Simuhealth
note: Simuhealth makes an enterprise platform that automates healthcare simulation, training, and compliance programs, with clients including several BC health authorities. The CAD 2.6 million pre-seed round exceeded its original CAD 2 million target and will fund expansion in Canada and the US.

name: Tuhk
note: Tuhk is a financial cybersecurity startup whose platform pools siloed data into a single intelligence network to help banks, merchants, and payment providers detect and shut down payment fraud. The all-equity seed round, which closed Dec. 3, will fund market entry in the UK, US, and Canada.

name: Amiral Ventures
note: Montréal-based venture firm founded by repeat entrepreneurs Frédéric Bastien, Dominic Becotte, and Nectarios Economakis aims to lead seed and Series A rounds in enterprise AI, robotics, and supply-chain tech. The first close of its targeted CAD 75 mil fund raised CAD 40 mil, with the Québec government anchoring through Investissement Québec.

name: Lumo Analytics
note: Lumo Analytics builds laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) scanners that rapidly analyze the mineral composition of drill core samples. Calgary's GeologicAI is acquiring Lumo and its team, with financial terms not disclosed, to complete its critical minerals sensing suite.

name: McRock Capital
note: McRock Capital, a Toronto VC firm focused on industrial tech, reached a final close of over CAD 120 million on its third fund, short of its CAD 200 million target but its largest to date. New LPs include Caterpillar and Autodesk, joining EDC, BDC Capital, and others.

name: Photonic
note: Photonic is developing networked quantum computers that use entanglement to link machines and plans to sell quantum computing services to enterprises. The $180M CAD first close brings its total raised to $375M CAD, and the CEO expects to raise up to $250M USD more within three months.

name: Backboard.io
note: Backboard.io builds a portable memory layer that lets users plug the context of their AI chats into more than 2,000 LLMs across vendors. The company, founded in April 2025 by Assent co-founder Rob Imbeault, raised an undisclosed pre-seed round that it describes as one of the largest pre-seed rounds in Canada in recent years.

name: Quantum Circuits
note: D-Wave Quantum agreed to acquire Quantum Circuits, a privately held gate-model quantum computing firm spun out of Yale in 2015, in a $550M USD deal ($300M in D-Wave stock and $250M in cash). The acquisition is expected to close later this month and will add gate-model capability to D-Wave's quantum annealing business.

name: Portage
note: Portage, the FinTech investment arm of Power Corp.'s Sagard, agreed to oversee Point72 Ventures' FinTech assets through a new $280M USD continuation vehicle managed by former Point72 partner Tripp Shriner, who joins Portage as a GP. The deal is Portage's first formal secondary investment, and Point72 keeps a 40 percent stake in the CV.

name: Slate
note: Slate is building embedded lending infrastructure that lets Canadian platforms offer loans to their SMB customers without building their own lending stack. The company closed the pre-seed round via a SAFE, with undisclosed strategic angels also participating, and says its lending platform is now live.

name: Science&Humans
note: Science&Humans is a Toronto telemedicine platform that connects Canadians with specialists for hormone health issues such as low testosterone, menopause, and weight management. The $10M CAD Series A includes $7M in equity and $3M in venture debt from CIBC Innovation Banking, and the company says it is generating seven figures in annual revenue.

name: Mangrove Lithium
note: Mangrove Lithium uses patented electrochemical technology to refine raw lithium from brines, hard rocks, and clays into battery-grade materials for EVs. The up-to-USD 85 mil structured financing includes up to USD 65 mil from the Canada Growth Fund, plus a CAD 9 mil loan underwritten by National Bank of Canada to fund its first commercial refinery in Delta, BC.

name: Dominion Dynamics
note: Dominion Dynamics, founded in June by former Anduril go-to-market lead Eliot Pence, builds Auranet, a software layer that connects Arctic hardware sensors into a data network for military monitoring. The seed round brings its total raised to $26 million, and the company did not disclose its valuation.

name: Jetson
note: Jetson makes the Jetson Air, a smart electric heat pump that connects to existing ductwork as a replacement for gas furnaces. The company says it has over CAD 4 million in monthly revenue since its September product launch, and it plans to use the funding to expand across the US and Canada.

name: 365Talents
note: 365Talents is a French upskilling platform that uses AI agents to map workforce skill gaps and guide employees toward roles and development opportunities. Toronto-based Docebo acquired it for about $54.6M USD, with an additional $5.1M USD payable on undisclosed milestones and expected 2026 revenue of about $9M USD.

name: Chata Technologies
note: Chata Technologies (Chata.ai) provides self-service analytics that lets users query financial and other data in natural language, using a CPU-based deterministic AI model rather than generative AI. The company closed a $10 million USD (about $13.8 million CAD) Series A to scale its platform across traditional finance, decentralized finance, and wealthtech.

name: Venture Scientist Fund (Mila and Inovia Capital)
note: Mila and Inovia Capital launched an early-stage fund to commercialize Canadian AI research, aiming to back at least 55 AI-native startups across Mila, Amii, and Vector Institute. Fundraising began immediately, and Mila expects to reach its target quickly.

name: Prévoir
note: Prévoir offers an AI and computer vision platform that extracts product attributes and links them to sales and inventory data to help fashion retailers curate collections and predict trends. The $750,000 CAD pre-seed round closed January 9 with Edmonton AI developer AltaML as the sole investor, and the company plans to use the funds to scale its platform and customer support.

name: Cyclic Materials
note: Cyclic Materials recycles end-of-life products, such as magnet production waste and magnet-containing scrap, to recover rare earth elements using physical and hydrometallurgical methods. The Series C, its largest round to date, will fund expansion across the US and Europe and its Canada-based R&D in Kingston, Ont.

name: Billdr
note: Billdr relaunched as a vertical SaaS platform for small and medium-sized general contractors after pivoting away from its homeowner renovation marketplace. The all-equity seed round, led by White Star Capital, brings its total funding to about USD 10.5 mil.

name: Birdseye
note: Birdseye, a Toronto startup that sells direct-mail marketing tools, received a $5M USD investment to spin out Yolando, an AI competitive-intelligence tool that tracks how businesses appear in results from large language models like ChatGPT and Gemini. The funding came from existing investor Drive Capital, its third investment in Birdseye, bringing its total commitment to $8.5M USD.

name: Float Financial
note: Float provides expense management, corporate cards, accounting services, and chequing-style business accounts for Canadian SMEs. The company secured the debt through two facilities, $75 million from Silicon Valley Bank (now a division of First Citizens Bank) and $20 million from an undisclosed Canadian Schedule I bank, to scale its interest-free Charge credit product.

name: Cellar Insights
note: Cellar Insights uses remote storage monitoring and machine learning to detect early spoilage risk and shrinkage in stored potatoes, aiming to reduce post-harvest loss. The company raised $500,000 CAD in early-stage funding from the SVG Ventures Pioneer Fund, which will support commercialization.

name: Waabi
note: Waabi is a Toronto-based autonomous vehicle startup building a physical AI platform for self-driving trucks and, now, robotaxis. The all-equity Series C is described as the largest fundraise in Canadian tech history, with Uber committing up to a further USD 250 mil in milestone-based funding.

name: Neo Financial
note: Neo Financial is a Canadian FinTech company that closed a $68.5 million CAD equity round in mid-January, alongside a new securitization program to fund lending growth. The round included AIMCo, Northleaf Capital Partners, Sandstone Asset Management, Plaza Ventures, and Caldwell Growth Opportunities, and was reportedly almost entirely Canadian-funded.

name: Acterys
note: Acterys is an operational planning and app development platform that lets IT teams write data into Power BI and unify analytics across Microsoft Fabric. Toronto-based Vena Solutions is acquiring it in a cash-and-stock deal, expected to close this quarter, with the price undisclosed and Acterys reportedly profitable, growing 100% year over year, and at about $13M USD in ARR.

name: BDC Capital life sciences fund
roundsize: a little more than CAD 100 mil (not yet confirmed)
note: BDC, Canada's largest VC investor, is preparing a new life sciences fund to make direct medtech investments and fill a financing gap from early to late stage. The fund is expected to launch before April, and its size has not been confirmed.

name: Brilliant Harvest
note: Brilliant Harvest is an AI platform that ingests technical manuals, work orders, and conversational data to answer questions for service, parts, and aftermarket teams in the heavy equipment industry. The seed round, announced Feb. 5, includes returning investors Builders VC and AltaML and new participants FTW Ventures, Alpaca VC, Automotive Ventures, SVG Ventures, and NYA Ventures.

name: Fieldless Farms
note: Fieldless Farms, an Ottawa indoor leafy greens grower that operates a facility in Cornwall, Ont., was acquired by Toronto-based Elevate Farms on Jan. 23. The deal price was not disclosed, and the companies say the combination will expand Canadian food security and international reach.

name: pHathom Technologies
note: pHathom Technologies makes shore-based carbon capture technology that bolts onto coastal bioenergy plants and converts CO2 into bicarbonate for ocean storage. The company closed a CAD 4 million seed round via SAFE across multiple closes, with plans to pilot the technology in Atlantic Canada.

name: Haply Robotics
note: Haply Robotics makes haptic controllers and a hardware-software platform that lets robots and AI systems sense and respond to physical forces in real time. The company closed a seed-plus equity round to fund expansion, manufacturing, and hiring, bringing its total raised above CAD 20 million.

name: Kaster Technologies
note: Kaster Technologies makes software that builds optimized production plans for drug manufacturers, claiming up to 20% more capacity without new equipment. The $1.6M CAD pre-seed equity round was led by Graphite Ventures, with the funds going toward refining the software and growing the six-person team.

name: Kiwi Charge
note: Kiwi Charge is developing an autonomous EV-charging robot that serves multi-unit housing and car dealerships, currently piloting with GM Canada and Pfaff Automotive in a $1.7-million project. The company expects to close a $1-million seed round led by an undisclosed American investor sometime in March.

name: Lenders API
note: Lenders API, a four-person consortium-based platform that helps non-prime consumer, small business, and auto lenders detect coordinated lending fraud, was acquired by Edmonton's Trust Science. Financial terms were not disclosed, and Trust Science is integrating Lenders API into its AI-driven risk and decisioning infrastructure.

name: Modem
note: Modem, founded by former Sentry VP of engineering Ben Vinegar, builds agentic AI that plugs into software teams' existing platforms to flag bugs, curate support tickets, and follow up with customers after updates. The equity pre-seed round was led by Accel, with Inovia Capital and angels including Cohere co-founder Ivan Zhang and Sentry co-founders participating; Sentry is also a client.

name: Kainova Therapeutics
note: Kainova (formerly Domain Therapeutics) is developing cancer and inflammation drugs that target G protein-coupled receptors, with its lead antibody DT-7012 in a Phase I/II trial. The CAD 32 million is the first close of its Series B, led by Investissement Québec, and will fund DT-7012 and preclinical work on the oral candidate DT-9046.

name: Kuzu
note: Kuzu develops a lightweight embedded graph database and was founded in 2023 by a group including former CEO Semih Salihoğlu, a University of Waterloo professor. Apple disclosed to the EU that on Oct. 9, 2025, it agreed to buy all Kuzu shares and hire select employees through an unnamed subsidiary, with no financial terms disclosed.

name: Shakudo
note: Shakudo sells software that helps companies deploy AI tools inside their existing infrastructure using their own data, and describes itself as 'the operating system for AI.' The all-equity Series A2 round, closed in late October, was led by Wittington Ventures and included customers such as CentralReach's CEO, bringing total funding to about USD 18 million.

name: Mecademic
note: Mecademic makes palm-sized industrial robots for component manufacturing, electronics, medical devices, and biopharma, and lists SpaceX, NASA, and Meta as customers. The company raised a $21 million strategic round led by Investissement Québec, with participation from EDC and BDC, to expand its headquarters and hire in the US, Europe, and Asia.

name: Toyo
note: Toyo is building an agentic AI platform that lets non-technical small business founders delegate CRM, email automation, and website building to AI agents. The company raised $4.3 million USD ($5.9 million CAD) in seed funding on a SAFE, which it announced after pivoting from its earlier product Layercode.

name: General Magic
note: General Magic builds agentic AI texting agents that handle insurance customer interactions, from quoting and eligibility to claims, so customers avoid long hold times. The $7.2M USD round was led by Radical Ventures with significant participation from a16z speedrun, bringing total funding to $8.4M USD.

name: Novacap
note: Novacap, a Montréal private equity firm managing $12 billion USD, closed its seventh tech-focused buyout fund, its largest yet, after exceeding its $2.75 billion USD target in under a year. The fund will keep the firm's strategy of taking majority stakes in profitable tech companies, with an average cheque of $300 million USD.

name: Wyvern
note: Wyvern operates the Dragonette constellation of hyperspectral imaging satellites and is developing next-generation Rosette satellites with deployable optics. NordSpace, a Canadian aerospace company, made an undisclosed strategic investment in Wyvern through its newly launched NordSpace Ventures arm, which is Ventures' first portfolio investment.

name: JetScale AI
note: JetScale AI builds agentic AI software that connects to clients' cloud accounts, finds inefficiencies such as idle resources and outdated databases, and delivers reviewable remediation code. The CAD 5.4 million seed round brings its total funding to CAD 6 million and will fund product expansion and growth across North America and Europe.

name: Wolf Advanced Technology
note: Wolf Advanced Technology, founded in 1999, makes rugged embedded computing systems for aerospace and defence customers. It received a repayable federal contribution (a zero-interest loan) of more than $8 million through FedDev Ontario's Regional Defence Investment Initiative to build in-house production, inspection, and validation capabilities.

name: Covelya Group
note: Covelya Group, a UK-based underwater technology conglomerate with six subsidiaries including Sonardyne and EIVA, designs maritime defence and commercial subsea systems. St. John's-based Kraken Robotics agreed to acquire it for $615 million, paid with $480 million cash and $135 million in Kraken shares, to expand its defence offering.

name: Spellbook
note: Spellbook makes AI tools for contract drafting, review, and the full contract-to-signing workflow, used by lawyers, procurement, and sales teams. The company secured a $40M USD line of credit to fund acquisitions of smaller contract-focused legal AI competitors, and expects to buy about five companies within two years.

name: UniUni
note: UniUni runs a gig worker-powered e-commerce logistics and last-mile delivery platform that uses passenger vehicles, acting as a delivery partner for AliExpress, Shein, and Temu. The USD 85 mil package combines USD 30 mil in equity, led by Beijing-based Rockets Capital, with a USD 55 mil credit facility from Royal Bank of Canada.

name: Staircase Ventures
note: Staircase Ventures, an early-stage VC firm that backs Canadian pre-seed and seed tech startups, closed its second fund at $50 million CAD, above its $40 million target. More than 80 percent of Fund I's limited partners returned, and new backers include BDC Capital, InBC Investment Corp, and the University of Alberta's endowment fund.

name: Alan
note: Alan is a French insurance technology company that sells health insurance to employers and provides virtual healthcare through its app, and it has expanded into Canada. The EUR 100 million round values the company at more than EUR 5 billion and will fund its international expansion, including Canada.

name: MDA Space
note: MDA Space, a Brampton-based space hardware manufacturer, is listing on the NYSE under the ticker MDA while keeping its Toronto Stock Exchange listing. The offering priced at $30.50 USD per share for more than 9.8 million shares, and proceeds will fund growth, possible acquisitions, and some debt repayment.

name: BDC StrongNorth Fund
note: The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) launched a $300-million deep tech fund, the StrongNorth Fund, to back startups developing defence and dual-use technology. The fund is part of BDC's Defence Platform, which expanded to about $6 billion after a $1.2-billion federal top-up, and it plans 30 to 40 startup investments of $1 million to $20 million over four years.

name: Gumloop
note: Gumloop sells an enterprise platform that lets employees build their own AI agents by connecting internal data to AI models, with customers including Ramp, Shopify, and Instacart. The $50M USD Series B was led by Benchmark, and part of Shopify Ventures' earlier investment converted into the round.

name: Walter

Healthcare-acquired infections such as C. diff affect roughly one in 38 hospital patients daily per US CDC. Founders started in the US because it's simpler to sell into a private system.

name: Intellistake / NanoAi
note: Vancouver AI infrastructure company Intellistake agreed to acquire Dallas-based NanoAi Technologies for $17M CAD in stock, issued against performance milestones tied to NanoAi's future revenue and contracts. Intellistake wants NanoAi's proprietary standoff detection devices, which identify viruses, explosives, and illicit drugs in the air without physical contact. Still subject to IP and financial due diligence; expected to close within 60 days.

name: Aureka Biotechnologies
note: AI-native drug discovery platform (protein therapeutics). 3 years old; $200M raised to date. Proceeds to train its model via a lab-in-the-loop feedback mechanism.

name: Point2 Technology
note: Builds interconnect solutions for AI data centers. Extension of its Series B, with a strategic investment from Arm Holdings.

name: Epicrispr Biotechnologies
note: Developer of genetic medicines; develops treatments for neuromuscular disease through modulating genes.

name: Neros Technologies
note: Defense drone manufacturer and drone interceptor. Founded 2023; $370M raised to date. Plans to build 1 million drones/year by 2028; contracts with US military and allied countries.

name: River AI
note: Founded earlier this year; raised $1.1B across seed and Series A. Founder Igor Babuschkin (ex-Google DeepMind, OpenAI, xAI). Building AI personalized and trained directly on what a company or person needs.

name: Bridge to Life
note: 21-year-old organ preservation company developing an organ viability assessment tool. Proceeds to extend its VitaSmart technology to US transplant centers.

name: CodeRabbit
note: Open-source AI code review technology used by 150,000 open-source projects and 17,000 customers. Plans a London office based on European customer interest.

name: Form Energy
note: Builds longer-lasting 100-hour batteries for grid electricity storage. Broad investor syndicate spanning PE, venture, angels and climate-focused funds.

name: Lovable
note: Non-US round. Automated application builder valued at $13.3B; claims 900M visits/month and 60M projects created. Series B (Dec 2025) valued it at $6.6B.

name: Databricks
note: Surpassed a $7B revenue run rate with 80%+ YoY growth in Q2; round raised its valuation to $190B (up from $134B in Dec 2025). ~$25B raised all-time since its 2013 Series A.

name: Cambridge Aerospace
note: Non-US round. UK defense tech; 2 years old. Raised a $200M Series B in April. UK Ministry of Defence committed to buy its Skyhammer air defense system to intercept drones and low-speed missiles.

name: Groq
note: Operator of 13 data centers globally; values company at $3.5B. Comes on the heels of a $650M round in June.

name: Higgsfield
note: AI video- and image-creation platform; closed at a $5.4B valuation, with the financing drawing at least 18 investors.

name: Wispr Flow
note: Provider of an AI-powered voice-to-text tool called Flow; picked up funding at a $2B valuation.

name: Etched
note: Developer of inference clusters to accelerate AI computing. Round set a $21B valuation for the 4-year-old company.

name: Happy Health
note: Developer of a ring device for diagnosis and treatment of sleep apnea.

name: Velaura AI
note: Developer of AI compute infrastructure focused on ultra-low-power silicon and software; round set a valuation of over $1B.

name: Also
note: Rivian spinout making electric bikes and small four-wheeled micromobility vehicles. Financing to accelerate development of its autonomous vehicle platform.

name: Castelion
note: Defense tech startup developing a hypersonic strike missile. Series C of $800M equity plus $250M debt; set a $13B valuation.

name: Rillet
note: Developer of AI-powered enterprise resource planning (ERP) tools; round sets a $1B valuation. Rillet's third financing in the past year.

name: Muon Space
note: Designer, builder and operator of satellite constellations. Recently opened a San Jose facility designed to produce up to 500 satellites annually by 2027.

name: Blank Street
note: Coffee and matcha drink chain planning a West Coast expansion. Also raised $30M in secondary market transactions.

name: Generalist AI
note: Developing an AI foundation model that can work with a variety of robots. Extension of its $400M Series B in June.

name: Emerald AI
note: Software platform that balances AI computational workloads and available energy resources. Financing set its valuation at $1.05B.

name: Gatik
note: Operator of driverless trucks; closed Series D for the 9-year-old company.

name: Stability AI
note: Developer of AI products for professional creatives across music, gaming and entertainment.

name: Instinct
note: Developing and beta-testing an AI assistant; raising at a $2.5B valuation (per WSJ, citing founder Noah Shinn).

name: AusperBio
note: Developing therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B and other diseases. Funding supports clinical trials for its lead therapeutic.

name: Regent Craft
note: Developer of high-speed winged sea vessels; $120M Series B equity plus $120M debt from Erebor Bank.

name: Socure
note: Provider of identity, risk and compliance tools; raised $156M growth funding at a $5.2B valuation and acquired Fravity, an agentic fraud/compliance platform.

name: Owner
note: AI tools for local businesses to automate websites, online/phone ordering, mobile apps and customer support. Values the 8-year-old company at $2.3B.

name: Fluidstack
note: Provides large-scale GPU and data center infrastructure for demanding AI workloads. Round values the company at $18B; total funding now just over $2.6B.

name: Upwind Security
note: Cloud security platform using real-time runtime data to identify threats and vulnerabilities. Valued at $3.8B; $730M raised to date.

name: David
note: High-protein food company best known for its high-protein, low-calorie bars, expanding into other protein-focused foods. Valued at $2.25B; $335M raised.

name: Gimlet Labs
note: Building an AI inference cloud that distributes workloads across different chip types to make running AI models faster and more efficient. Valued at $3B; $392M raised to date.

name: HiBob
note: Bob platform combines HR, payroll, benefits and employee management; positioning workforce data as a foundation for enterprise AI. Valued at $3.2B; total funding $740M.

name: HiddenLayer
note: Builds security tools specifically to protect AI models, agents and workflows from attacks and vulnerabilities as enterprises move AI into production. $156.2M raised to date.

name: Lyte AI
note: Founded by former Apple engineers; develops custom silicon, sensors and AI software that help robots perceive their surroundings. Valued at $1.6B; $272M raised to date.

name: TabaPay
note: Money-movement infrastructure that helps banks and fintechs instantly disburse, collect and transfer funds. Announced alongside a planned acquisition of Transact Bank.

name: Thyme Care
note: Works with health plans, employers and providers to coordinate cancer treatment and manage oncology care under value-based specialty care. Valued at $2B; $399M raised total.

name: Celero Communications
note: Develops coherent digital signal processor technology that moves large quantities of data between chips and data centers using less power. Valued at $3B; total funding ~$413.4M.

name: Cognition
note: Best known for Devin, its autonomous software-engineering agent. Valued at $48B; nearly $3.9B raised to date.

name: Stoke Space
note: Developing fully reusable rockets including its Nova launch vehicle to lower the cost of transporting payloads to orbit. Valued at $10B; total funding ~$2.4B.

name: Suniva
note: Longtime U.S. solar manufacturer producing high-efficiency solar cells; new capital to expand domestic production including a new South Carolina facility. Nearly $1.2B raised to date.

name: Encoded Therapeutics
note: Clinical-stage biotech developing precision genetic medicines for severe neurological disorders; lead therapy targets Dravet syndrome. $514.1M raised to date.

name: Fab2
note: Formerly Atomic Semi; rethinking semiconductor manufacturing by designing its own fabrication tools, components and software to build smaller chip factories faster and cheaper. First disclosed round; valued at $3.7B.

name: Harvey
note: Builds generative AI tools for lawyers and professional-services workers: legal research, document analysis and contract work. Valued at $15.5B; total funding nearly $1.8B.

name: The Boring Co.
note: Elon Musk's tunnel-drilling company building underground tunnel networks; already operates the Vegas Loop under Las Vegas. Valued at $23B; total funding nearly $3.9B.

name: Mach Industries
note: Founded 2022; defense manufacturer developing unmanned aircraft, long-range weapons and propulsion technology. Valued at $3.7B; total funding nearly $1.1B.

name: Motive
note: Formerly KeepTruckin; AI-driven platform used by trucking, construction and other physical-economy businesses to manage fleets and automate operations. Total funding just over $2B.

name: Positron
note: Develops purpose-built hardware for AI inference, challenging GPUs in particular AI workloads. Total $875M raised across a $375M Series C ($3.5B pre-money) plus a Series C-1 of up to $500M led by NEA and Jim Clark; $5B post-money valuation. (Crunchbase roundup listed only the $500M tranche.)

name: Temporal Technologies
note: Developer of an open-source platform for building and operating long-running AI agents and other enterprise systems. Valued at $12.55B.

name: Impulse Space
note: Developer of space vehicles for moving payloads across and between orbits. Extension brings the combined round total to $808M.

name: Ridgeline
note: AI-enabled investment management platform. Round set a $1.45B valuation.

name: Crusoe
note: Data center and AI cloud provider originally founded to power crypto mining with stranded natural gas; now serves OpenAI, Microsoft and Meta. Round values it at $30B (triple its valuation of a year ago); ~$7.2B raised to date.

name: Arcee AI
note: Developer of open-weight AI models. Valued at more than $1B.

name: Cornelis Networks
note: Develops networking technology for AI and high-performance computing workloads.

name: Factory
note: Provider of AI tools for enterprise software development. Round set a $5B valuation.

name: Mazama Energy
note: Geothermal energy developer specializing in superhot rock geothermal power.

name: Nex
note: Developer of family-oriented digital games that rely on body motion rather than controllers. New equity and debt financing; equity portion not broken out.

name: Profound
note: Offers marketing software to help users appear more prominently in AI results. Valued at $1.8B.

name: Sling Therapeutics
note: Developer of a small-molecule therapy for thyroid eye disease.

name: Cyera
note: Provider of enterprise data security tools that govern both humans and AI agents. Total funding now $2.7B.

name: Snorkel AI
note: Provides tools for frontier labs and AI teams to develop specialized training data and environments. Valued at $3.2B; more than $375M in ARR.

name: Enveda
note: AI-enabled drug discovery startup. Round brings total capital raised since inception to more than $845M.

name: Axya
note: Axya builds an AI-powered procurement platform that integrates with manufacturers' ERP systems and connects them to suppliers, serving clients like GE Aerospace and MDA Space. The CAD 17 million Series A comprises CAD 12 million in equity led by McRock Capital, with Yamaha Motor Ventures and existing backers participating, plus CAD 5 million in venture debt from CIBC Innovation Banking.

name: Island
note: Developer of tools for secure enterprise digital operations. Round set a $6.4B valuation, more than double its 2024 valuation.

name: Precision Neuroscience
note: Focused on brain-computer interface technology.

name: Hubble Network
note: Operator of a satellite network that extends connectivity to Bluetooth devices. Round set a $1.6B valuation.

name: Micro1
note: Provider of AI training data to major AI labs. Reportedly raised more than $100M at a $4B valuation, per Forbes citing people familiar with the deal.

name: Numeral
note: AI-powered sales tax compliance platform.

name: Rainmaker
note: Focused on atmospheric research and producing new freshwater through cloud seeding.

name: Rightway
note: Provider of pharmacy benefits and care navigation services; financing in part to expand its AI capabilities.

name: UniUni
note: UniUni, a last-mile delivery company that uses gig workers and passenger vehicles, entered a term sheet for a new private funding round after SPAC partner MAK Acquisition Corp sent a notice of breach over its deteriorating finances. The round is led by an undisclosed existing investor, and the amount was not disclosed.

name: Brodie Rec
note: Brodie Rec runs a recreational basketball app and league with over 50,000 active players across 35 cities, using video, stats, and AI tools to make adult play feel like a sports career. The company raised $5 million CAD last December, per the article, and is on track for $10 million in revenue this year and profitability next year.

name: Daedal Systems
note: Daedal Systems, founded by a former General Fusion employee, builds standardized plasma measurement systems so fusion developers don't have to build diagnostics in-house. The just over USD 4 million round will fund its first three reactor diagnostic systems and pilot deployments.

name: Plurilock
note: Plurilock is a cybersecurity firm that started with behavioural biometrics and now offers security technology and advisory services to enterprise and government clients. Montréal-based Quantum eMotion (QeM) is acquiring all of Plurilock's outstanding shares for nearly CAD 34 million, paid 30% cash and 70% in QeM common shares, pending a Plurilock shareholder vote in November.

name: Freddie (parent: PurposeMed)
note: Freddie offers physician-led telehealth, HIV testing, and PrEP services in Canada and all 50 US states. Grindr agreed to acquire PurposeMed, Freddie's parent, for $250 million USD ($190M cash plus $60M in Grindr stock), with an additional performance-based payment in 2028, and the deal is expected to close in Q4 2026.

name: H2 Analytics
note: H2 Analytics builds the Exercise Architect Suite (EASE), a military and emergency training exercise platform. FedDev Ontario announced $800,000 CAD in repayable funding toward a more than $4.2 million project to add AI features and support international expansion.

name: One Silicon Chip Photonics (OSCP)
note: OSCP develops chip-based photonic gyroscopes and IMUs that let autonomous vehicles and robots navigate when GNSS/GPS is jammed or unavailable. The all-equity Series A closed in August and will fund commercialization and next-generation products.

name: Kin Commerce
note: Toronto-based Reactiv acquired New York-based competitor Kin Commerce, which builds AI-powered mobile apps for e-commerce brands such as Steve Madden and Chubbies. The cash deal closed in early September 2026 for an undisclosed price, and included Kin's tech, IP, customers, and one engineer, while Kin's founders pivoted to a new AI marketing startup.

name: Mecka AI
note: Mecka AI collects first-person human video and sensor data from real-world settings and converts it into training data for robotics labs and Big Tech firms. The company raised a USD 60M Series B led by Sequoia Capital, with new backers including Nvidia, Microsoft's and Qualcomm's venture arms, and Samsung.

name: Senso
note: Senso, a Toronto company that began with predictive retention tools for credit unions, built a generative engine optimization (GEO) tool that helps brands appear in AI-generated search answers. New York-based Zeta Global agreed to acquire Senso and bring its technology and team, including CEO Saroop Bharwani, in-house; the price was not disclosed.

name: Oso Cloud
note: Oso Cloud makes authorization management software that helps businesses track access controls for humans and AI agents. Victoria-based holding company Tiny acquired its assets for $1.9 million CAD, with Oso's co-founder and CEO Graham Neray and team members joining Temporal Technologies.

name: Bia Health
note: Bia Health builds the Bia Assistant, an AI tool that helps clinicians choose diagnostic plans and avoid unnecessary imaging, referrals, and interventions. The CAD 2.15 million raise includes CAD 1.4 million in debt from Finalta Capital, with the equity portion led by Anges Québec.

name: Aisle
note: Aisle, a Prague-based AI company that builds tools to find and fix software vulnerabilities, is being acquired by Toronto's Cohere under a letter of intent. Aisle's roughly 50 employees will join Cohere, and its CEO will lead a new Cohere Cyber unit.

name: Molagri
note: Molagri develops easily updatable pesticides synthesized on a non-infectious insect virus that can be tweaked to stay ahead of pest resistance. The $5.2M USD ($8.2M CAD) seed round was led by Convective Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, Superorganism, Robinhood Ventures, and Paul Graham.

name: Aerium
note: Aerium is a Toronto-based AI platform that integrates with industrial manufacturers' and distributors' existing systems to centralize siloed data and deploy AI agents and machine learning models to monitor operations and automate tasks. The company raised USD 2.5 million (about CAD 3.6 million) in seed funding via a SAFE that closed in July.

name: Inovia Capital
note: Inovia Capital completed a USD 200 million first close of its sixth early-stage VC fund, which targets USD 325 million and will focus on AI-native and frontier technology startups. The returning LPs supporting the close include BDC, CDPQ, CIBC, Fondaction, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Investissement Québec, and Teralys Capital.

name: Tenstorrent
note: Tenstorrent builds AI compute hardware, from single cards to superclusters, and licenses its AI and RISC-V IP to clients such as LG and Samsung. The Series E sets a post-money valuation of USD 6.2 billion, more than double its USD 2.6 billion valuation at its late-2024 Series D.

name: Hive
note: Hive builds a marketing platform that connects venue and event promoter data with email, text, advertising, and CRM tools, using AI to automate marketing. The $27M USD Series B is mostly secondary capital that bought out early investor Avenue Growth Partners, with a small primary component for product and go-to-market.

name: Vistara Growth
note: Vancouver private credit firm Vistara Growth launched its sixth fund, an evergreen vehicle that provides debt and equity to mid- and later-stage North American tech companies. It targets USD 500 million, with an initial close of USD 200 to 250 million hoped for by the end of November.

name: Wealthsimple
note: Wealthsimple, a Toronto robo-adviser that has expanded into banking and other money management services, agreed to up to $425M CAD from existing investors at a $13.8B post-money valuation. The deal includes $300M in new primary equity for its product and technology roadmap and a $125M secondary sale of employee shares.
